translations.text: The vision of Isaiah son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, who ruled over Judah.
Listen, heaven, and give ear, earth, for the Lord has spoken: “I fathered children and raised them up, but they dishonored me.”
The ox knows its owner, and the donkey its master's manger, but Israel did not know me, and my people paid no attention to me.
Woe to the sinful nation, the people full of sins, the wicked offspring, the lawless children! They abandoned the Lord and angered the Holy One of Israel. They became estranged and turned back.
Why do you keep adding wounds to your lawlessness? Every head is in pain, and every heart is in sorrow.
From the feet to the head there is no soundness in it: no wound, no swelling, no festering injury. There is no ointment to apply, no oil, and no bandages.
Your land is desolate, and your cities are burned. Foreigners devour your country before your eyes; it is laid waste and overthrown by foreign nations.
The daughter of Zion will be left abandoned, like a hut in a vineyard, like a shelter for fruit-watchers in a melon field, and like a besieged city.
If the Lord of hosts had not left us offspring, we would have become like Sodom and resembled Gomorrah.
Hear the word of the Lord, rulers of Sodom! Give ear to the law of God, peoples of Gomorrah!
“What do your many sacrifices mean to me?” says the Lord. “I have had enough of the burnt offerings of your rams. I do not want the fat of lambs or the blood of bulls and goats.”
“Not even when you come to appear before me! Who asked this of you, that you should trample my courts?”
“Do not keep bringing offerings to me; it is futile. Your incense is an abomination to me. I do not accept your new moons, your Sabbaths, or the great day, your fasting and your idleness, and”
“my soul hates your new moons and your festivals. I have had enough of you; I will no longer tolerate your sins.”
“When you lift up your hands, I will turn my face away from you. Even if you multiply your prayers, I will not listen to you, because your hands are full of blood.”
“Wash yourselves and make yourselves clean. Remove your evil deeds from yourselves before my eyes. Cease your evil deeds.”
“Learn to do good. Seek justice. Rescue the oppressed. Judge the orphan's case, and give the widow justice.”
“Come, let us speak with one another,” says the Lord. “Even if your sins are like scarlet, I will make them white as snow; even if they are red like crimson, I will make them clean as wool.”
“If you are willing and listen to me, you will eat the good things of the land.”
“But if you refuse to listen to me, the sword will devour you,” for the mouth of the Lord has spoken this.
How has the faithful city, Zion, full of faithfulness, become a prostitute? Righteousness once rested in her, but now there are murderers.
Your silver fails the test; your merchants mix water with wine.
Your rulers are rebels and accomplices of thieves. They love bribes and take revenge. They do not give orphans justice and do not listen to widows' cases.

Therefore thus says the Lord, the Lord of hosts, the Mighty One of Israel: “Woe to you, mighty ones of Israel! My anger against my adversaries will no longer cease, and I will judge my enemies with judgments.”
“I will lay my hand upon you and bring you into the heat to cleanse you of your rebels. I will destroy your rebels, remove all the lawless from you, and humble all the proud.”
And I will appoint judges over you as at first, and your counselors as in the beginning. Then you will be called the city of righteousness, the faithful mother of cities, Zion.
For her captive people will be redeemed through justice and righteousness and mercy.
The lawless and sinners will be crushed together, and those who abandoned the Lord will perish together.

For now they will be ashamed of their idols, in which they took pleasure. They will be clothed in shame because of the carved images they themselves made, and they will be ashamed of their gardens, which they desired.
For they will be like a terebinth that has shed its leaves, and like a garden that has no water.
Their strength will become like beaten flax, and their works like sparks of fire. The lawless and sinners will burn together, and there will be no one to put out the fire.
The word that came to Isaiah son of Amoz concerning Judea and Jerusalem.
For in the last days the mountain of the Lord will be manifest, and the house of God will stand upon the mountain peaks and be raised above the hills. All nations will come to it.

Many peoples will go and say, “Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, to the house of the God of Jacob. He will tell us his ways, and we will walk with him.” For laws will go out from Zion, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.

He will judge among the nations and rebuke many peoples. They will forge their swords into plowshares and their spears into sickles. Nation will not take up a sword against nation, and they will no longer learn to wage war.
And now, you house of Jacob, come, let us walk in the light of the Lord.
For he abandoned his people, the house of Jacob, because their land was filled, as before, with divinations like those of foreigners, and many foreign children were born to them.
Their land was filled with gold and silver, and there was no counting their treasures. Their land was filled with horses, and there was no counting their chariots.
Their land was filled with abominations, the works of their own hands. They bowed down to what their own fingers had made.
Humanity was humbled, and man fell to the ground, and I will not forgive them.
And now go, enter beneath the rocks and hide in the earth from the terror of the Lord and from the glory of his power, when he rises to strike the earth.
For the eyes of the Lord are high, but man is brought low. Human loftiness will be humbled, and the Lord alone will be exalted on that day.
For the day of the Lord of hosts will be against everyone who is proud and arrogant, and against everyone who is exalted and lifted up, and they will be humbled.
And against all the cedars of Lebanon, exalted and lifted up, and against all the oak trees of Bashan.
And against all the high mountains and against all the lofty hills.
And against all the lofty towers and against all the lofty walls.
And against all the ships of the sea and against every display of the beauty of ships.
All humanity will be humbled, and human pride will fall, and the Lord alone will be exalted on that day.
They will take away everything they have made with their hands.
They will hide them in caves, in the crevices of rocks, and in holes in the earth, from the terror of the Lord and from the glory of his power, when he rises to strike the earth.
For on that day a person will cast away his abominations of silver and gold, which they made to bow down to worthless things and bats.
To enter the holes of solid rock and the clefts of the rocks, away from the terror of the Lord and the glory of his might, when he rises to shake the earth.
Keep away from man, whose breath is in his nostrils, for among whom should he be counted?
Look, the Lord, the Lord of hosts, will remove from Judea and Jerusalem the mighty man and the strong woman, the strength of bread and the strength of water,
the giant and the strong man, the warrior and the judge, the prophet and the examiner and the elder,
and the captain of fifty, the admirable counselor, the wise master builder, and the discerning listener.
And I will appoint children as rulers over them, and deceivers will rule over them.
And the people will fall upon one another, each man against his neighbor; the young will clash with the old, and the dishonorable with the honorable.
For a man will seize his brother or a member of his father's household and say, “You have clothing. Be our ruler, and let our food be in your care.”
He will answer on that day and say, “I will not be a ruler, for there is neither bread nor clothing in my house, and I will not be a ruler of this people.”
For Jerusalem has been abandoned and Judea has fallen, and their tongues have rebelled against the Lord through lawlessness.

Therefore their glory has been brought low, and the shame of their faces has covered them. They have proclaimed their sins like the people of Sodom and made them known. Woe to their souls, for they have devised an evil plan for themselves!
And they say, “Let us bind the righteous man, for he has become disagreeable to us.” From now on they will eat the fruits of their own deeds.
Woe to the lawless man! Evils will come upon him according to the deeds of his hands.
My people, your tax collectors strip you bare, and those who demand payment rule over you. My people, those who call you blessed deceive you and throw the paths of your feet into confusion.
But now the Lord will come to judgment and bring his people before the court.
The Lord himself will enter into judgment with the elders of his people and their rulers: “Why have you burned my vineyard? What you have plundered from the poor is in your houses.
Why do you oppress my people and fill the faces of the poor with shame?” says the Lord, the Lord of hosts.
Thus says the Lord: “Because the daughters of Zion have become proud and walk with their necks held high, signaling with their eyebrows, dragging their hems as they walk, and dancing with their feet,
God will bring low the rulers of the daughter of Zion, and the Lord will strip away their adornment.”
On that day the Lord will remove the splendor of their clothing and their robes,
and their braids, hair clasps, crown bands, and crescent ornaments,
and the adornment of their faces, the embellishments of their splendid finery, their veils, bracelets, necklaces, and earrings,
and their rings and [?], their brocades and [?],
the garments with purple borders and those with purple centers, the coverings worn at home, and the conspicuous Laconian garments.
The fine linen, the sky-blue cloth, the red [?], the striped cloth, the gold-striped cloth, and the gold [?].

And instead of sweet fragrances there will be dust, and instead of belts, a rope girdle; instead of golden head ornaments, baldness because of your deeds; and instead of gold-woven brocade, you will wear sackcloth.
And your beautiful son, whom you love, will die by the sword, and your rulers will fall by the sword.
And the chests of your ornaments will become desolate and be clothed in mourning, and you will remain alone and fall to the ground.
And seven women will seize one man and say, “We will eat our own bread and wear our own clothing. Only let your name be given to us; take away our disgrace.”
On that day God will shine forth with his glorious purposes upon the earth, to exalt and glorify the remnant of Israel.
And those who remain in Zion and those who remain in Jerusalem will be called holy—all who are recorded in Jerusalem for life.
For the Lord will wash away the filth of the sons and daughters of Zion and of Jerusalem, and cleanse the blood from her midst by a spirit of judgment and a spirit of burning.

And he will come, and over every place on Mount Zion and everything around it there will be a covering of cloud by day, and something like smoke and the light of a blazing fire by night. Everything will be covered with glory.
And there will be shade from the heat and a sheltering roof against harsh weather and rain.
I will sing to my beloved vineyard the song of its beloved. The beloved had a vineyard on a hillside, in a fertile place.
I enclosed it with a fence, furnished it with stakes, and planted a Sorek vine. I built a tower in its midst and dug a winepress pit in it. I waited for it to produce grapes, but it produced thorns.
And now, men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem, judge between me and my vineyard.
What was there to do for my vineyard that I did not do for it? I waited for it to produce grapes, but it produced thorns.
And now I myself will tell you what I will do to my vineyard. I will tear down its fence, and it will be plundered. I will demolish its walls, and it will be trampled.
I will abandon my vineyard. It will not be pruned or hoed, and thorns will grow in it as on uncultivated land. I will command my clouds not to rain on my vineyard.

For the vineyard of the Lord of hosts is the house of Israel, and the people of Judah are his beloved new planting. I waited for them to practice justice, but they practiced injustice—not righteousness, but an outcry.
Woe to those who join house to house and bring field close to field, so as to drive out their neighbor! Will you alone dwell in the land?
Look, all this was reported in the ears of the Lord of hosts: even if there are many houses, they will become desolate; even if they are large and beautiful, there will be no one to live in them.
For where ten yoke of oxen work, there will be only one jar, and whoever sows six artabs will gather three grivs.
Woe to those who rise early in the morning and pursue strong drink, who linger over it until evening, for the wine itself burns them!
They drink wine with pipes, drums, harps, and songs, but they do not look at the deeds of the Lord or consider the works of his hands.
Therefore my people were handed over into captivity because they did not know the Lord, and many of them became corpses for lack of bread and from thirst for water.

And the underworld has enlarged itself and opened its mouth without ceasing. Their glorious ones, their great ones, their wealthy ones, their evildoers, and those who rejoice among them will descend into it.
Humanity will be humbled, and men will be dishonored, and arrogant eyes will be brought low.
And the Lord of hosts will be exalted through justice, and the holy God will be glorified through righteousness.
And those who have been plundered will graze like bulls, and lambs will feed on the ruins of those who remain.
Woe to those who drag their sins as with a long rope, and their lawless deeds as with a strap from a heifer’s yoke!
They say, “Let what he is going to do come quickly, so that we may see it! Let the plan of the Holy One of Israel come, so that we may know it!”
Woe to those who call evil good and good evil, who make light darkness and darkness light, who make bitter sweet and sweet bitter!
Woe to those who consider themselves wise and are discerning in their own eyes!
Woe to your mighty men who drink wine, and to your rulers who mix strong drink!
who acquit the wicked for bribes and rob the righteous of their rights.

Therefore, as a reed catches fire from sparks, so they will burn in a blazing flame. Their root will become like chaff, and their blossom will rise like dust, because they rejected the law of the Lord of hosts and also provoked the Holy One of Israel by rejecting his words.

The Lord of hosts became fiercely angry with his people, stretched out his hand against them, and destroyed them. He grew angry against the mountains, and their corpses became like dung along the road. Despite all this, his anger has not turned away, and his hand is still raised.
After this he will raise a signal for distant nations and bring them from the ends of the earth. Look, they will run swiftly and arrive speedily.
They will neither hunger nor grow weary; they will neither doze nor sleep. They will not loosen the belts around their waists, nor will the straps of their sandals break.
Their arrows are sharpened and their bows drawn. Their horses’ hooves are reckoned as solid rock, and the wheels of their chariots are like a whirlwind.
They will advance like lions and come like young lions. They will roar, charge, and tear savagely, and there will be no one to rescue them.

On that day they will raise a cry over them like the sound of a sea raging with waves. They will look up to heaven and down to the earth, and there will be the darkness of distress in their bewilderment.
And in the year in which King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord seated on a high and exalted throne, and the house was full of his glory.
Seraphim stood around him. Each had six wings: with two they covered their faces, with two they covered their feet, and with two they flew.
They cried out to one another and said, “Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hosts; the whole earth is full of his glory.”
The lintel rose at the sound of their cries, and the house filled with smoke.

And I said, “Woe to me! I am a miserable man. How I stand astonished! For I am a man with unclean lips, and I dwell among a people with unclean lips, yet I have seen the Lord of hosts with my own eyes.”
One of the seraphim was sent to me, holding in his hand a burning coal that he had taken from the altar with tongs.
He brought it to my mouth and said, “Look, this has touched your lips. It will take away your lawlessness and cleanse you of your sins.”
I heard the voice of the Lord saying, “Whom shall I send, and who will go to that people?” And I said, “Here I am; send me.”
He said, “Go and tell that people: ‘You will hear, but do not understand; you will see, but do not comprehend.’

For the heart of this people has grown dull. Their ears have become hard of hearing, and they have closed their eyes, lest they ever see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, and turn back, and I heal them.”
And I said, “Until when, Lord?” He said, “Until the cities are emptied of inhabitants, the houses have no people, and the land is left desolate.
After that, God will send people far away, and those left in the land will multiply.
Yet a tenth will be taken from it, and they will again go into captivity and be plundered, like a terebinth and like an acorn shaken from their respective husks. The holy offspring is its monument.”

In the days of Ahaz son of Jotham, son of Uzziah, king of Judah, Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up against Jerusalem to wage war against it, but they could not besiege it.
The house of David was informed, “Aram has joined forces with Ephraim.” His heart and the heart of his people trembled like a tree in the forest stirred by the wind.
The Lord said to Isaiah, “Go out to meet Ahaz, you and your surviving son Jashub, opposite the upper pool, on the road to the fuller’s field.”

And you shall say to him, “Be careful, remain calm, and do not be afraid. Do not let your soul be terrified by these two smoking pieces of charred wood, for when the anger of my wrath comes, I will heal again. And the son of Aram and the son of Remaliah”
For Ephraim and the son of Remaliah have devised an evil plan against you, and they say,
“Let us go up to Judah, speak with them, turn them toward us, and appoint the son of Tabeel as their king.”
Thus says the Lord of hosts: “That plan shall not stand, and it shall not come to pass.”
But the head of Aram is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin. In another sixty-five years, the kingdom of Ephraim will cease to be a people.
And the head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is the son of Remaliah. If you do not believe, neither will you understand.
And the Lord spoke again to Ahaz and said,
Ask for yourself a sign from the Lord your God, in the depths or in the heights.
And Ahaz said, “I will not ask, nor will I put the Lord to the test.”
And he says, “Now listen, house of David! Does it seem a small thing to you to weary people? And how is it that you weary the Lord?”
Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign: Behold, the virgin will conceive and bear a son, and they will call his name Immanuel.
He will eat butter and honey; before he knows or desires evil, he will choose what is good.
Therefore, before the child knows good or evil, he will reject evil and choose good, and the land that you fear because of the two kings will remain.
But God will bring upon you, upon your people, and upon your father’s house days such as have not yet come since the day he took Ephraim away from Judah—the king of Assyria.
And on that day the Lord will stir up the fly that rules beyond the river of Egypt and the bee that is in the land of Assyria.
And they will all come and settle in the valleys of your land, in the clefts of the rocks, in caves, in every hollow, and in every tree.
On that day the Lord will shave with the great, drunken razor that is beyond the river—the king of Assyria—the head and the hair of the feet, and he will remove the beard.
And on that day a man will raise one heifer from the cattle and two ewes.
And because of the abundance of milk, he will eat butter, for everyone who remains in the land will eat butter and honey.
And on that day every place where there are a thousand vines worth a thousand shekels in weight will become wasteland and turn to thorns.
Archers and bowmen will enter there, because the whole land will become wasteland and bear thorns.
And every mountain will be plowed and broken into furrows, and no fear will come there, for from wasteland and thorns it will become pasture for lambs and ground trampled by oxen.
And the Lord says to me, “Take for yourself a large new scroll and write on it with the pen of a skilled man: ‘Quickly, quickly take the spoil, and swiftly gather the plunder, for it has arrived.’”
And you shall appoint trustworthy men as witnesses for me: Uriah the priest and Zechariah the son of Berechiah.
And I approached my wife, the prophetess, and she conceived and bore a son. And the Lord said to me, “Call his name ‘Plunder Quickly and Take Spoil Speedily.’”
For before the child knows how to call his father or his mother, he will take the wealth of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria before the king of Assyria.
And the Lord spoke to me again and said,
“Because this people did not desire the water of Shiloah, which flows gently, but wanted to make Rezin and the son of Remaliah their kings,
therefore, behold, the Lord will bring upon you the mighty and abundant water of the River—the king of Assyria and his glory. It will come and reach all your valleys and pass over your walls.”
And he will remove from your land of Judea the man who can lift his head and the strong man who can accomplish anything, and his army will fill the breadth of your land.

God is with us. Know this, you nations, and be defeated. Listen, all the way to the ends of the earth. You mighty ones, be defeated, for even if you grow strong again, you will again be delivered into defeat.
Whatever plan you devise, the Lord will scatter it, and whatever word you speak, it will not stand for you, because the Lord God is with us.
Thus says the Lord to those who, by the strength of his hand, turn against following the way of this people:
And they say, “Never speak harshness, for everything this people says is harshness.” Do not fear what they fear, and do not be troubled.
You shall regard the Lord of hosts himself as holy, and he shall be the one you fear. And if you put your hope in him—

He will be a sanctuary for you, and your foot will not strike a stone, nor will you encounter a stumbling block. But the house of Jacob will be in a snare and in the pits of those lying in ambush in Jerusalem.
For this reason many will become weak through him; they will fall and be broken, and people dwelling in the settlement will come under siege.
At that time those who seal the laws will be revealed,
so that no one may learn. And he will say, “I will stand and wait for God, who has turned his face away from the house of Jacob, and I will put my hope in him.”
Here I am, and the children whom God has given me. They will be signs and wonders upon the house of Israel from the Lord of hosts, who dwells on Mount Zion.

And if they say to you, “Consult the sorcerers, the necromancers, the babblers, and the ventriloquists”—should not a people consult its own God? Why should they consult the dead on behalf of the living?
For he gave the laws as a help, so that they might say, “Not like these words, concerning which no bribes can be given on their behalf.”
And a severe famine will come upon you. When you become hungry, you will be distressed and curse the ruler and the land, and they will lift their eyes upward to heaven

and look downward to the earth. And behold, want and suffering, darkness, affliction, anguish, and gloom, so that no one can see. And let anyone who is in affliction not lose heart until the appointed time.

But first drink this; quickly follow, land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, the way of the sea, and you others who dwell along the seacoast and beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations, the regions of Judea.
The people who walked in darkness saw a great light, and upon you who dwell in the land and in the shadow of death, light will dawn.
The great portion of this people, whom you brought down into your joy—they will rejoice before you as people rejoice at harvest and as those who divide the spoil.
For the yoke that lay upon them and the rod upon their neck have been removed from them, for he cast away the rod of their oppressors, as on the day of Midian.
For they will pay penalties for every robe and garment gathered by deceit. But they wished that they had been burned.

For a child was born to us, a son was given to us, whose authority rested on his shoulders, and his name was called Messenger of Great Counsel, Wonderful, Counselor, Mighty God, Ruler, Father of the world to come.

And I will bring peace upon his rulers and health to him. Great is his dominion, and his peace has no limit. He will sit on the throne of David and make his kingdom prosper, strengthening it with justice and righteousness from this time onward and forever. The zeal of the Lord of hosts will do this.
The Lord sent death upon Jacob, and it came upon Israel.
And all the people of Ephraim and those who dwell in Samaria will know it, those who spoke with pride and arrogance of heart and say:
“The bricks have fallen, but come, let us cut stones. Let us strike down the cedars and fir trees and build ourselves a tower.”
And God will destroy those who rise up against Mount Zion and scatter the enemies of Judah,
Assyria from the east and the Greeks from the west, who devoured Israel with their mouths wide open. Despite all this, his anger has not turned away, but his hand is still raised.
And the people did not turn back until they were wounded, and they did not seek the Lord of hosts.
And the Lord removed from Israel the head and the tail, the great and the small, in one day.
The elder and the respected person are the head, and the prophet who taught lawlessness is the tail.
And those who call this people blessed will be led astray, and they will lead them astray so that they may devour them.

Therefore God will not rejoice over their young men, nor will he have mercy on their orphans and widows, for they are all lawless and wicked, and every mouth speaks injustice. Despite all this, his anger has not turned away, but his hand is still raised.
And lawlessness will blaze like fire and burn like dry grass in the fire. It will spread into the cedar forests, and fire will consume everything around their hills.
Because of the Lord’s furious anger, the whole land will be set on fire, and the people will be burned as by fire. Let no man have mercy on his brother.
But he will turn to his right because of hunger and eat on his left, yet he will not be satisfied, each man eating the flesh of his own arms.
For Manasseh will devour Ephraim, and Ephraim Manasseh, and together they will besiege Judah. Despite all this, his anger has not turned away, but his hand is still raised.
Woe to those who write wicked things; in writing, they write their own wickedness.
They pervert the judgments of the poor and rob the needy of my people of their rights, so that the widow becomes their plunder and the orphan their spoil.
And what will they do on the day of visitation? For your affliction will come from far away. To whom will you flee for help, and where will you leave your glory,
except to be handed over into captivity and to go down beneath the slain? Despite all this, his anger has not turned away, but his hand is still raised.
Woe to the Assyrian, the rod of my anger and wrath in their hands,
for I will send my anger against a lawless nation, and I will command my people to take plunder and spoil, to trample cities and reduce them to dust.
But he did not think this way or consider it this way within himself. Instead, he turned his mind to destroying many nations.
And if they say to him, “Are you alone a ruler?”
he will say, “Have I not taken the land beyond Babylon and Calneh, where the tower was built? I also took Arabia, Damascus, and Samaria.
Just as I took them with my own hand, so I will take all the kingdoms. Wail, carved images in Jerusalem and Samaria!
For just as I did to Samaria and its handmade images, so I will do to Jerusalem and its idols.”
And when the Lord has finished doing everything on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, he will also bring anger upon the arrogant one, upon the ruler of the Assyrians and upon the proud glory of his eyes.
For he said, “I will do it by my own strength and by the wisdom of my plans. I will remove the boundaries of nations and take their forces as plunder; I will shake inhabited cities.”

I will reach with my hand over the whole world as over a nest, and gather up the eggs left behind. There will be no one who escapes me, no one who turns against me, opens his mouth, or makes a chirping sound.
Thus says the Lord: Can an axe rise without a woodcutter, or a saw be lifted without someone drawing it? Likewise, if someone takes a rod or a piece of wood, it is not so.
But the Lord of hosts will send dishonor upon your honor, and a burning fire will blaze amid your glory.
The Light of Israel will become a fire and purify him with burning fire, and will devour the forest like grass.
On that day the mountains, hills, and forests will be extinguished, and it will consume from soul to body. The survivor will be like someone who has escaped a blazing flame.
Those remaining among them will be few enough to count, and a little child will write them down.
On that day the remnant of Israel and the survivors of Jacob will no longer continue to rely on their oppressors, but will rely in truth on God, the Holy One of Israel.
And the remnant of Jacob will be with the mighty God.
Even if the people of Israel are like the sand of the sea, only a small remnant of them will remain.
For the word is brief and concise in righteousness; the Lord of hosts will make the word concise throughout the whole world.

Therefore this is what the Lord, the Lord of hosts, says: “Do not fear the Assyrians, my people who dwell in Zion, even if they strike you with a rod; for I bring blows upon you to make you know the way of the Egyptians.”
For in a little while the anger will cease, but my wrath will be against their schemes.
And the Lord God will raise blows against them like the blows against Midian at the place of torment, and his wrath will be like that along the way through the sea at the departure of the Egyptians.
On that day his terror will be lifted from you, and his yoke from your neck, and the yoke will be shattered from your shoulders.
For he will reach the city of Ai and pass through Megiddo, and at Michmash he will set down his equipment.
He will pass through the valleys and come upon the Gibeonites. Terror will seize Ramah, the city of Saul; the daughter of Gallim will flee.
Cry out with your voice; let it be heard in Laish, let it be heard in Anathoth.
Madmenah will be terrified, as will those who live in Gerim.
Today he will be encouraged to lodge on the road; with his hand he will encourage the mountain, the daughter of Zion, and the hills that are in Jerusalem.
For behold, the Lord, the Lord of hosts, will throw the glorious ones into turmoil with his power, and those raised high in arrogance will be shattered and humbled.
The heights will fall by the sword, and Lebanon will be brought down with its lofty heights.
A shoot will spring from the root of Jesse, and a flower will come forth from that root.
The Spirit of God will rest upon him: the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and strength, the spirit of knowledge and godliness.
The spirit of the fear of God will fill him. He will not judge by appearances or rebuke according to what people say.
But he will uphold the rights of the poor and rebuke the lowly of the earth. He will strike the earth with the word of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips he will destroy the ungodly.
Righteousness will be wrapped around his waist, and his sides will be girded with truth.
The wolf will graze with the lamb, and the leopard will lie down beside the young goat. The calf, the bull, and the lion will graze together, and a little child will lead them.
The ox and the bear will graze together, and their young will roam together. The lion will eat straw like the ox.
A little child will put his hand into a viper’s hole and into the nest of young vipers.

And they will do no wrong, nor will they be able to strike anyone on my holy mountain, for the whole earth has been filled with the knowledge of the Lord, like the abundant waters that cover the seas.
And on that day there will be the root of Jesse, who is to rise as ruler of the nations. In him the nations will hope, and his resting place will be honored.

And on that day the Lord will again show his hand, zealously reclaiming the remnant of his people who remain among the Assyrians, the Egyptians, the Babylonians, the Ethiopians, the Elamites, those in the east, the Arabs, and those on the islands of the sea.
And he will raise a banner among the nations and gather the lost of Israel, and he will gather the scattered of Judah from the four corners of the earth.
And Ephraim’s envy will be removed, and Judah’s enemies will perish. Ephraim will not envy Judah, and Judah will not envy Ephraim.

And the ships of the foreigners will fly, and together they will plunder the coast and the people of the east and the Edomites. They will first lay their hands on Moab, and the sons of Ammon will submit before them.
And the Lord will destroy the sea of the Egyptians and stretch his hand over the river with a fierce wind. He will strike its seven channels so that it can be crossed confidently, even with shoes on.
And there will be a passage for the remnant of my people who are in Egypt, and it will be for Israel as on the day when they came out of the land of the Egyptians.
And you will say on that day, “I will bless you, Lord, for you were angry with me, but you turned your wrath away from me and had mercy on me.”
Behold, my God is my savior, the Lord. I will trust in him and will not fear, for the Lord is my glory and my praise, and he has become my salvation.
And draw water with joy from the springs of salvation.
And on that day you will say: Bless the Lord; proclaim his name; tell of his glories among the nations; remember that his name has been exalted.
Bless the name of the Lord, for he has done great things. Tell this to the whole earth.
Rejoice and be glad, inhabitants of Zion, for the Holy One of Israel has been exalted in her midst.
The vision concerning the Babylonians, which Isaiah son of Amoz saw.
Raise a banner on the level mountain; lift your voice against them. Do not be afraid. Beckon with your hand. Open up, rulers, and I will give the command.
They are consecrated, and I will bring them. Giants come rushing to satisfy my wrath; together they come rejoicing and acting with contempt.
The sound of many nations upon the mountains, like the sound of many nations; the sound of kings and [?] gathered together. The Lord of hosts has given a command to armed nations
to come from a distant land, from the ends of the foundations of heaven. The Lord has arrived with his armed warriors to destroy the whole world.
Wail, for the day of the Lord is near, and destruction from God has arrived.
Therefore every hand will grow weak, and every human soul will tremble.
The angels will be troubled, and birth pains will seize them like women in labor. They will flare up against one another and become furious, and their faces will turn flame-colored.
For behold, the day of the Lord has arrived, terrible, full of anger, vengeance, and wrath, to make the world a wilderness and destroy the sinners from it.
For the stars of heaven, together with Orion and all the adornment of heaven, will give no light. The sun will be darkened as it rises, and the moon will not give its light.
And I will decree evils against the whole world, and punishment for the ungodly for their sins. I will destroy the pride of the lawless and bring down the arrogance of the boastful.
And those who remain will be more precious than unrefined gold, and a human being will be more precious than the precious stones of Ophir.
For the heavens will rage, and the earth will be shaken from its foundations because of the fierce anger of the Lord of hosts, on the day when his wrath arrives.
And those who remain will be like a fleeing gazelle and like a wandering sheep, with no one to gather them. Each person will return to his own people, and each man will be driven to his own land.
For whoever is caught will be handed over to defeat, and those who are gathered will fall by the sword.
And they will slaughter their children before their eyes, plunder their houses, and violate their wives.
Look, I am raising up against you the Medes, who consider silver and gold to be nothing.
They will shatter the bows of the young men and have no mercy on your sons, and their eyes will not spare your children.
And Babylon, which is called glorious by the king of the Chaldeans, will be as when God destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah.
It will not be inhabited for all time, and no one will enter it for many generations. Arabs will no longer pass through it, and shepherds will not rest there.
Instead, wild beasts will rest there, and their houses will be filled with cries. Sirens will rest there, and demons will dance there.
Donkey-centaurs will live there, and hedgehogs will bear their young in its palaces. It has drawn near and is coming quickly; it will not be delayed, and its days will not be prolonged.
The Lord will have mercy on Jacob and will choose Israel again. They will rest in their own land, and the foreigner will join the house of Jacob.

The nations will receive them and bring them to their own places, and they will inherit and multiply in God's land as male and female slaves. Those who took them captive will become captives, and those who ruled them will fall into servitude.
And on that day the Lord will give you rest from your pain, from your anger, and from the harsh slavery in which you served them.
And you will take up this lament over the king of Babylon and say on that day, “How the tribute collector has ceased! The oppressor is at rest!”
For the Lord has shattered the yoke of sinners, the yoke of rulers.
He destroyed the nations in fury, with unbearable blows, in merciless anger.
The whole earth rests in hope and cries out with joy.
The trees of Lebanon trampled on you, and the cedars of Lebanon say, “Since you ceased, no woodcutters have come up against us.”
The underworld below grew bitter at meeting you. All the giants who had been rulers of the earth stood up together, those who raised all the kings of the nations from their thrones.
They will all answer you and say, “Were you too seized like us and counted among us?”
Your glory and your great joy have gone down to the underworld. They will spread moths beneath you, and worms will cover you.
How the Morning Star, which rose at dawn, has fallen from heaven! It has fallen to the earth and been shattered, the one who sent to all the nations.
You said in your mind, “I will ascend to heaven; I will set my throne above the stars of heaven. I will sit on the high mountain, above the lofty mountains of the north.
I will ascend above the clouds; I will be like the Most High.”
But now, behold, you will descend into the underworld and to the foundations of the earth.
Those who see you will be astonished at you and say, “Is this the man who enraged the earth and shook kings,
who made the whole world a wasteland and demolished its cities, and did not let the captives return from captivity?”
All the kings of the nations have lain down in honor, each man in his own house.
But you will be cast upon the mountains like a loathsome corpse, among the many corpses of those slain by the sword who descended into the underworld, like blood-soaked rags that are not clean.
Likewise, you too will not be cleansed, because you ruined my land and slaughtered my people. May you not remain forever, evil offspring!
Prepare your sons for slaughter because of the sins of their fathers, so that they may not rise and inherit the earth and fill the earth with wars.
“I will rise against them,” says the Lord of hosts, “and I will destroy their name, their descendants, and their offspring.” Thus says the Lord of hosts.
“I will make Babylon a wasteland, so that hedgehogs will live there. It will come to nothing, and I will make it a muddy pit of destruction.”
Thus says the Lord of hosts: “As I have said, so it will be, and as I have planned, so it will stand.”
To destroy the Assyrians in my land and on my mountains; they shall be trampled underfoot, and their yoke shall be lifted from you, and their arrogance shall be removed from your neck.
This is the plan that the Lord has devised concerning the whole world, and this is the hand raised over all nations.
For who can undo what the holy God has planned? And who can turn back his raised hand?
In the year in which King Ahaz died, this pronouncement came against the Philistines.

Do not rejoice, all you foreigners, because the yoke of those who struck you has been broken. For offspring of vipers will come from the serpent’s descendants, and winged serpents will come from their offspring.
The poor shall be nourished by him, and weak people shall dwell in peace. He shall destroy your offspring by famine, and he shall destroy your survivors.
Wail, gates of the cities! Let the cities cry out, all you troubled foreigners! Smoke has risen from the north, and it will no longer be found.
And what answer shall the kings of the nations give? That the Lord has established the foundations of Zion, and through it the lowly among the people shall be saved.
A pronouncement against the Moabites. In the night the Moabite shall be destroyed; in the night the wall of Moab shall be demolished.
Mourn for yourselves, for Dibon, the site of your temple, has perished. Go up there to weep, to Nebo of the Moabites. Wail, for every head is bald and every arm is broken.
Put on sackcloth in its squares, mourn on its rooftops, and all of you lament with weeping in its streets.
For Heshbon and Elealeh cried out, and their voices were heard as far as Jahaz. Therefore Moab’s [?] cries out, and he shall know his own soul.

The heart of Moab cries out within him as far as Zoar, for she is a three-year-old heifer. They shall ascend to you weeping by the ascent of Luhith; on the road to Horonaim he cries out about destruction and upheaval.
The water of Nimrim will diminish and dry up, its grass will dwindle, and no green plant will be found there. Can he be saved even so?
For I shall bring the Arabs upon the valleys, and they shall take it.
For the outcry from the borders of Moab joined the cries of the people of Gallim, and its lamentation reached as far as the well of Elim—its lamentation.

And the water of Rimmon shall be filled with blood, for I shall bring the Arabs upon Rimmon and remove the offspring of Moab and Ariel; and I shall send the survivors of Admah across the land like creeping creatures.
Shall the mountain of the daughter of Zion be a desolate rock?
And you, daughter of the Moabites, shall be like a chick left behind by a bird that has flown away.
But now you too, Arnon, consider further how to make shelters for their mourning. Let them continually flee at midday as though through darkness.

They were terrified, and you shall not drive them away, for the fugitives of Moab shall reside with you, and they shall be a refuge for you from the persecutor. For your companion in battle has been removed, and the ruler who trampled the land has perished.
And a throne shall be established through mercy, and someone shall sit upon it in truth in the dwelling of David. He shall judge and seek justice and hasten to act righteously.
We have heard of Moab’s arrogance, for he was exceedingly proud—his pride and his resentment—and your arrogance shall be taken away from you.
It shall not be as your divination foretells, nor as the lamentation in Moab. For in Moab everyone shall lament. You shall grumble about those who dwell in Deseth, and you shall not feel shame.

The fields of Heshbon shall mourn, and the vineyards of Sibmah, which swallowed up the nations. Trample its vineyards as far as Jazer, and do not reach it. You have wandered in the wilderness; those sent by it were abandoned, for they crossed the sea.
Therefore I shall weep for the vineyards of Sibmah as Jazer weeps. Heshbon and Elealeh cut down your planted trees, for I shall trample your harvests and your vintage, and all shall be destroyed.
And joy and gladness shall be removed from the vineyards. Let there be no joy in your vineyard, and let them not tread wine in your winepresses, for it has ceased.
Therefore my inward parts shall resound like a harp over Moab, and you have renewed my belly like a wall.
And this shall bring you shame, for Moab has exhausted himself in his shrines, and he shall enter as a worshiper among his handmade objects, but they shall not be able to save them.
This is the word that the Lord spoke long ago concerning Moab.

And now he spoke again and said, “Within three years, counted according to the years of a hired worker, Moab’s glory will be dishonored in all its great abundance, and what remains will be small and without honor.”
A pronouncement concerning Damascus. Look, Damascus will be removed from among the cities and will become a ruin.
Abandoned forever, it will become a sheepfold for flocks and a resting place for herds, and there will be no one to drive them away.

There will no longer be a fortified refuge for Ephraim, nor will a kingdom remain in Damascus, nor will the survivors of the Syrians remain, for you are no better than the children of Israel and their glory. Thus says the Lord of hosts.
On that day Jacob’s glory will diminish, and the abundance of his glory will be shaken.
It will be as when someone gathers standing grain into his arms and a gleaner goes behind him, and as when someone gathers ears of grain in the Valley of Firmness.

Stubble will remain in it, or it will be like the fruit of an olive tree: two or three olives at the tops of its highest branches, or four or five remaining on its boughs. Thus says the Lord God of Israel.
On that day a person will put his hope in his Creator, and his eyes will look to the Holy One of Israel.

They will no longer put their hope in temples or in the works of their hands, which their fingers made. Instead, they will put their hope in the Holy One of Israel, and they will no longer look to their groves or their abominations.
On that day your cities will be abandoned, just as the Amorites and the Hivites abandoned theirs before the children of Israel, and they will become ruins.
Because you abandoned God your Savior and did not remember the Lord your helper, you will therefore plant an unfaithful plant and unfaithful seed. On the day when you plant, you will fail.
If you sow in the morning, it will blossom in summer, on the day when you bestow an inheritance, like a father who leaves an inheritance to his children.
Woe to the multitude of many nations! Like the sea heaped up in waves, so you will rage, and the muscles of many nations will roar like water.

Like many waters are the many nations, like the force of torrents of abundant water. He will drive them away and chase them far off, like straw chaff swept away before the wind and like the dust of a wheel whirled about by a storm.
In the evening they will fall into mourning; before morning they will be no more. This is the portion of those who plunder you and the inheritance of those who took possession of you.
Woe to the land in the wings of ships, beyond the river of the Ethiopians!

It sent offerings across the sea and parchment letters over the waters [?], so that swift messengers might go to a proud nation, to a foreign and evil nation, for there is no one beyond it, to a hopeless and trampled nation.
And now, all the rivers of the earth: their land will be inhabited like an inhabited country. It will be raised like a signal from a mountain and will be heard like the sound of a trumpet.
For thus the Lord said to me: “There will be vigilance in my city, like scorching light at midday and like a cloud laden with dew in the days of summer.”

Before the harvest, when flowering is complete and the unripe grape blossoms, the blossom becoming an unripe grape, he will cut off the tiny grape clusters with a sickle, and he will cut the shoots and sever them.
He will leave them all together to the birds of heaven and the beasts of the earth. The birds of heaven will gather over them, and all the beasts of the earth will come upon them.

At that time offerings will be brought to the Lord of hosts from an oppressed and humbled people, and from a great people, from then on and for all time—a hopeful and trampled nation beside the river of its land—to the place where the name of the Lord of hosts has been invoked, on Mount Zion.
A vision concerning the Egyptians. Look, the Lord, seated on a light cloud, will come to Egypt. The handmade idols of the Egyptians will tremble before him, and their hearts will fail within them.
The Egyptians will rise against the Egyptians and wage war, each man against his brother and each man against his neighbor, city against city and law against law.
The spirits of the Egyptians will be troubled within them, and I will scatter their plans. They will consult their gods and their images, those who summon the dead, and sorcerers.
I will hand the Egyptians over to harsh-hearted masters, and harsh kings will rule over them. Thus says the Lord of hosts.
The Egyptians will drink from the pools along the seashore, for the river will diminish and dry up.
The rivers and the river's channels will diminish, and all the gathered waters will dry up, throughout all the meadows, all the thickets of reeds and rushes, and the marshy fields.
All the greenery around the river and all the cultivated fields watered by the river will be scorched by the hot wind and dry up.
The fishermen will grieve, and all who cast hooks into the river will sigh. Those who fish with nets and seines will mourn.
The workers in fine linen and those who weave fine cloth will be put to shame.
All the craftsmen will be filled with sorrow, and all their garment makers will grieve, and their hearts will ache.

The rulers of Tanis, the king's wise counselors, will become foolish, and their plans will become foolish. How can you say to the king, 'We are sons of wise men and sons of kings who lived from the beginning'?
Now where are your wise men? Let them tell you and declare what plan the Lord of hosts has devised against Egypt.
The rulers of Tanis have become foolish, and the rulers of Memphis have become proud. They will lead the Egyptians astray, tribe by tribe.
For the Lord has mixed into them a spirit of error, and they have led Egypt astray in all their deeds, as a drunken man who vomits staggers about.
There will no longer be any work for the Egyptians, either backward or forward, either at the beginning or at the end.
On that day the Egyptians will be like women, trembling and terrified before the hand of the Lord of hosts, which he himself will bring down upon them.

The land of Judah will become a terror to the Egyptians. Whenever anyone mentions the name of that land to them, they will be terrified because of the plan that the Lord of hosts has devised against it.
On that day there will be five cities in the land of the Egyptians that speak the language of the Canaanites and swear by the name of the Lord of hosts. One city will be called the City of Asedek.
On that day there will be an altar to the Lord in the land of the Egyptians and a pillar erected to the Lord at its border.

It will be an everlasting sign for the Lord in the land of the Egyptians, for they will cry out to the Lord because of their distress. The Lord will send them a man who will save them, and through judgment he will deliver them.
The Lord will become known to the Egyptians, and the Egyptians will know the Lord on that day. They will present sacrifices and offerings, make vows to the Lord, and fulfill them.
The Lord will strike the Egyptians with great blows, and he will surely heal them. They will return to the Lord, and he will hear them and heal them.
On that day there will be a road from the Egyptians to the Assyrians. The Assyrians will enter Egypt, and the Egyptians will go to the Assyrians, and the Egyptians will serve the Assyrians.
On that day Israel will be a third alongside the Egyptians and the Assyrians, blessed in the land.
whom the Lord of hosts blessed, saying, “Blessed be my people who are in Egypt and those among the Assyrians, and my inheritance, Israel.”
In the year when Tanathan came to Ashdod, after being sent by Arna, king of the Assyrians, he fought against Ashdod and captured it.
Then the Lord spoke to Isaiah son of Amoz, saying, “Go and remove the sackcloth from your waist, and take the sandals off your feet.” He did so and walked naked and barefoot.
And the Lord said, “Just as my servant Isaiah walks naked and barefoot, so for three years there will be signs and portents for the Egyptians and the Ethiopians.
They will understand that in this way the king of the Assyrians will lead the Egyptians and the Ethiopians into captivity, young and old, naked and barefoot, exposing the shame of the Egyptians.
The Egyptians, handed over to defeat, will be ashamed because of the Ethiopians, in whom the Egyptians had put their hope and who were their glory.

On that day the inhabitants of that island will say, ‘Look, we had hoped to find refuge in these people for help, but they could not even save themselves from the king of the Assyrians. How, then, will we escape?’”
A vision of the desert by the sea. Like a whirlwind passing through the desert, coming from the desert, from the land.

The vision is terrifying, and harsh things were reported to me: the one who is to despise despises, and the one who is to act lawlessly acts lawlessly. The Elamites have come against me, and the messengers of the Persians are coming against me. Now I will groan and comfort myself.
Because of this, my waist was filled with trembling, and pains seized me like a woman giving birth. I braced myself so that I would not hear; I hurried so that I would not see.
My heart turned to confusion, and lawlessness was still engulfing me. My soul stood trembling. Know your purpose.
Prepare a table; eat and drink. Rise, rulers, and prepare your shields.
For this is what the Lord said to me: “Go yourself and be a watchman, and report whatever you see.”
I saw two riders, one riding a donkey and one riding a camel. “Listen to the report with great attention, and call Uriah to the lookout post,” says the Lord.
I stood all day and all night watching over the camp.
And I saw that the same rider was coming with two horses. He answered and said, “Babylon has fallen and been overthrown, and all its images and its handmade objects have been smashed to the ground.”
Listen, you who remain and you who are afflicted. Listen to what I heard from the Lord of hosts, what the God of Israel told us.
A vision concerning the Edomites. Call to me from Mount Seir: “Guard the monuments.”
I will keep watch in the morning and at night. If you seek, seek, and dwell with me.
An oracle concerning the Arabs. In the evening you will sleep in the forest, on the road of the Dedanites.
Bring water to meet the thirsty, inhabitants of Tema; go out with bread to meet the fugitives.

Because of the multitude of those killed, because of the multitude of those wandering astray, because of the multitude of swords, because of the multitude of drawn bows, and because of the multitude of those fallen in battle.
For this is what the Lord said to me: “One more year, like the year of a hired worker, and the glory of the sons of Kedar will diminish.
The remaining mighty archers among the sons of Kedar will be few, for the Lord, the God of Israel, has spoken.”
A message concerning the valley of Zion. What is wrong with you? What has happened to you, that you have now all gone up onto the rooftops of vanity?
Your city is filled with bearers of bad news, your splendid city. Your wounded were not wounded by the sword, and your dead were not killed in battle.
All your rulers are fugitives, and your prisoners are harshly bound. Your mighty men were all bound together, openly fugitives.
For this reason I said, “Leave me alone to weep bitterly. Do not insist on comforting me over the ruin of the daughter of my people.”
For it is a day of turmoil and destruction, trampling and confusion, from the Lord of hosts in the valley of Zion. Great and small alike wander astray upon the mountains.
The Elamites have taken up their quivers, mounted on horses, with troops drawn up for battle.
Your choicest valleys will be filled with chariots, and horsemen will block your gates.
They will tear down the gates of Judah, and on that day they will see the choicest palaces of the city.
They will uncover the hidden things of the palaces on the heights of David. They saw that there were many, and that they had diverted the old aqueduct into the city,
and that they had demolished the palaces of Jerusalem to strengthen the city's walls.

You draw water for yourselves between the two walls, farther inside than the old aqueduct. Yet you did not look to the one who made it in the beginning, and you did not recognize the one who established it long ago.
On that day the Lord of hosts called for weeping and mourning, lamentation, shaving the head, and wearing sackcloth.
But they held celebrations and rejoiced. They slaughtered calves and killed sheep to eat meat and drink wine, saying, “Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die.”
This has been revealed in the ears of the Lord of hosts: “These sins will not be forgiven you until you die,” says the Lord of hosts.
Thus says the Lord, the Lord of hosts: “Go and enter the office there, to Shebna, the keeper of the wardrobe, and say to him,
‘Why have you come here, and what are you seeking here, that you have dug yourself a tomb here and made yourself a dwelling in this rock?’
Look, the Lord of hosts will drive you out and destroy you, O man, and will remove your robe and the crown of your glory.
He will cast you into a great and boundless land, and there you will die. He will turn your splendid chariots into a disgrace, and the house of your authority into something trampled underfoot.
You will be driven out of your office and from your established position.
On that day I will call my servant Eliakim son of Hilkiah.

I will clothe him in your robe and give him your crown in splendor. I will place your authority in his hands, and he will be like a father to the inhabitants of Jerusalem and the inhabitants of Judah.
I will give him the keys of David. He will rule, and no one will oppose him.
I will appoint him as ruler in a secure place, and he will become a throne of glory for his father's house.

All the honored members of his father's house will place their hope in him, from the least to the greatest, along with all the vessels, from the smallest to the basins. He will open, and no one will shut; he will shut, and no one will open. They will hang from him.

On that day, thus says the Lord of hosts: “The man established in a secure place will be shaken loose. He will fall and be brought down, and his glory will be taken away from him, for the Lord has spoken.”
An oracle concerning Tyre. Wail, ships of the Carthaginians, for they have perished and will no longer return from the land of Kittim. They have been carried away into captivity.
Whom have the inhabitants of that island come to resemble—the Phoenician merchants who cross the sea over many waters?
The offspring of the buyers are like the gathered produce of summer, the merchants of the nations.
Be ashamed, Sidon, says the sea. The strength of the sea will say, “I have not been in labor or given birth; I have not raised young men or brought up young women.”
When the news reaches the land of Egypt, anguish will seize them because of Tyre.
Go to Carthage; lament, you inhabitants of that island.
Was this not your pride from the beginning, before she was handed over? She will be carried away on her own feet into exile far away.
Who planned this against Tyre? Was she insignificant or weak? Her merchants were glorious among the Canaanites, and her traders were princes of the earth.
The Lord of hosts planned to tear down all the pride of the glorious and to dishonor everyone held in honor on the face of the earth.
Cultivate your land, for ships will no longer come from Carthage.
Your hand, with which you used to anger kings, will no longer prevail over the sea. The Lord of hosts has commanded that Canaan’s strength be destroyed.
They will say, “From now on, let us no longer abuse and oppress the virgin daughter of Zion.” But rise and cross the sea. Even if you go to Kittim, you will find no rest there.

Even if you go to the land of the Chaldeans, that too has been laid waste by the Assyrians, and you will find neither peace nor rest there. Sihim laid her foundation, erected her monuments, and raised her towers. Now her wall has fallen and been destroyed.
Wail, ships of the Carthaginians, for your stronghold has perished.
On that day Tyre will be abandoned for seventy years, like the span of one king's reign and like the span of one person's life. After seventy years, Tyre will be like the song of a prostitute.
Take a harp, wander about and lament, abandoned city of prostitution. Play well and sing often, so that your memory may remain.

After seventy years, the Lord will visit Tyre, and she will once again be restored to her former condition. Trade with all the kings of the world, across the whole face of the earth, will take place in her.

The proceeds of her trade will be dedicated to the Lord. They will not accumulate anything for themselves; instead, all her merchandise will belong to those who dwell before the Lord, so that they may eat, drink, and rejoice as a sign of remembrance before the Lord.
Look, the Lord will devastate the world and lay it waste, overturn its foundations, and scatter those who dwell in it.

The people will be like the priest, the slave like the master, and the maidservant like the mistress. The buyer will be like the seller, the lender like the borrower, and the debtor like the creditor.
The earth will be utterly devastated, and the earth will be thoroughly plundered, for the mouth of the Lord has spoken this.
The earth mourned and collapsed; the world collapsed and was devastated. The heights of the earth mourned.
For the earth became lawless through its inhabitants, because they transgressed the Lord’s laws, trampled on his commands, and broke the everlasting covenant.
Therefore curses will devour the earth, because its inhabitants have sinned. Therefore its inhabitants will become destitute, and few people will remain.
The wine will mourn, and the vineyard will mourn. All the revelers will sigh within themselves.
The joyful sound of tambourines fell silent; the pride and grandeur of the ungodly fell silent; the sounds of harps fell silent.
They were put to shame and did not drink wine. Strong drink became bitter to those who drank it.
All the cities were laid waste. The gates of the palaces were shut, because there was no one to enter.
Wail over the wine everywhere. All joy has fallen silent; all the earth’s joy has been vanquished.
The cities will be left desolate, and the remaining palaces will perish. All this will happen on the earth, among the nations.
Just as someone gleans an olive tree, so they will glean them. When the harvests cease, they will cry out loudly.
But those who remain on the earth will rejoice together in the glory of the Lord, and the waters of the sea will be stirred up.
Therefore glory belongs to the Lord in the islands of the sea, and the name of the Lord, the Lord God of Israel, will be glorified.

From the ends of the earth we have heard wonders, a hope for the godly. And they will say, “My secret is for me, my secret is for me and for my own.” Woe to those who despise, who show contempt and contemptuously despise the law!
Terror, a pit, and a snare are upon you, inhabitants of the earth!

And whoever flees from the terror will fall into the pit, and whoever comes out of the pit will be caught in the snare, for the windows of heaven have opened, and the foundations of the earth will shake.
The earth will be thrown into turmoil, and the earth will be utterly bewildered; it has bowed down.
The earth will shake violently like a fruit watchman’s hut. Like a drunkard and a staggering person, it will tumble and be unable to stand, because lawlessness has grown strong upon it.
And on that day God will lay his hand upon the host of heaven and upon the kings of the earth who are on the earth.
And they will gather his companies into bonds and confine them in fortresses, and after a long time they will be visited.
And the brick will melt, and the wall will collapse, for the Lord will reign on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, and he will be glorified before the elders.
Lord my God, I will glorify you and praise your name, for you have done wonderful things, fulfilling the ancient, true plan.
Yes, Lord, for you have turned cities into heaps of earth and fortified cities into ruins down to their foundations. May the city of the ungodly never be rebuilt.
Therefore a poor people will praise you, and the cities of oppressed people will praise you.
For you have become a helper to every lowly city and a shelter of refuge for those distressed by need. You rescued them from evil people.
A refuge for the thirsty and breath for oppressed people, like people faint and thirsty in Zion because of the ungodly people to whom you handed us over.

And the Lord of hosts will do this for all the nations on this mountain: they will drink joy, they will drink wine, they will anoint themselves with oil cleared of its sediment, and they will be swallowed up on this mountain.
Tell this to all the nations, for this is a plan concerning all peoples.

Death grew strong and devoured, and God again removed every tear from every face and took away the reproach of his people from all the earth, for the mouth of the Lord has spoken. He will lessen the heat with the shade of a cloud and lower the arms of the mighty.
And on that day they will say, “Look, this is the Lord our God, in whom we hoped, and he will save us. For he is the Lord, and we waited for him. Let us rejoice and be glad in our salvation.”
And God will give us rest on this mountain, and the Moabite will be trampled, just as someone tramples a threshing floor with threshing sledges.
And he will rest his hands; likewise, he too brought them to misery by destroying them. And he will bring down his pride, upon which he laid his hands.
And he will bring down the height of your protective walls, and they will descend to the ground.
On that day they will sing this song in the land of Judea: “Look, a fortified city! Our salvation will establish walls and ramparts.”
Open your gates, and let a people enter that keeps righteousness and keeps truth,
a guardian of truth, and it preserves peace, peace.
For we have placed our hope in you, Lord, forever.
You who humbled and brought down the inhabitants of the heights will destroy the mighty cities and bring them down to the ground.
The feet of the meek and lowly will trample them, the footsteps of the needy.
The paths of the devout are straight; the paths of those who worship God have been smoothed and prepared.
For the ways of the Lord are just judgments. We have hoped in your name and in your remembrance, with the longing of our spirits; our soul has desired you.
At night my spirit seeks you early, O God, for your commands are light upon the earth. Learn righteousness, inhabitants of the earth, for the wicked man has been silenced.
And everyone who does not learn righteousness on earth will not act truthfully. Let the ungodly be taken away, so that he may not see the glory of the Lord.
Lord, your arm is raised high, but they did not recognize it. They will recognize it and be ashamed, and jealousy will seize the undisciplined people. And now fire will devour the adversaries.
Lord our God, give us peace; you have rendered everything to us.
Lord our God, take possession of us. Lord, we know no one besides you, and we invoke your name.
But the dead will not see life, and physicians will not rise. Therefore you brought them, destroyed them, and wiped out all their males.
Add evils to them, Lord; add evils to the glorious ones of the earth. You have stretched out to all the ends of the earth.
Lord, in distress we remembered you, for your discipline is a slight affliction for us, and
as a woman in labor approaches childbirth and cries out in her pain, so we became to your beloved because of the fear of you, Lord.
We conceived, went into labor, and gave birth to the spirit of your salvation; we accomplished this upon the earth. We will no longer fall, but the inhabitants of the earth will fall.
The dead will rise, and those in the tombs will stand up and rejoice upon the earth, for the dew that comes from you is healing for them. But the land of the wicked will be overthrown.
Go, my people, enter your storerooms, shut your doors, and hide for a little while, until the Lord’s anger passes.
For behold, the Lord will bring anger from his holy place upon the inhabitants of the earth. The earth will reveal its blood and will not conceal those who have been slain.
On that day the Lord will bring his holy, great, and mighty sword against the dragon, the fleeing serpent, and against the dragon, the crooked serpent; and he will kill the dragon in the sea.
On that day there will be a beautiful vineyard, desirable to rule over.
I am a strong city, a city besieged in vain. I will water it, so that it will be taken at night, and by day its wall will be overthrown.

For there was no one who did not attack it. Who will appoint me to guard the [?] of the field in the countryside? Because of this warrior I despised it from now on. Therefore the Lord did everything that he had ordained. “We have been burned,” he says.
Its inhabitants will cry out, “Let us make peace with him.”
The gathered children of Jacob will sprout like new plants; Israel will blossom, and the world will be filled with its fruit.
Will this one be wounded as that one struck him? Or will he be destroyed as that one killed?
With warfare and reproaches he will send them away. Was it not you who planned, with a hardened mind, to kill them in a spirit of anger?

Therefore Jacob’s lawlessness will be removed, and this is his blessing: when I remove his sins from him, at the time when they grind all the stones of your temples into fine dust, the works of their worship will no longer remain, but will be cut down like cedars by woodcutters.

And the inhabited place that remains will be like a flock penned up and like abandoned livestock. For a long time it will be a pasture for wild animals, and they will rest there. After a long time no green herb will be found in it, for it has dried up.

Women who come hurrying from the spectacle, step forward, for this is not a people possessing wisdom. Therefore may God, who made them, not pity them, and may he who formed them not have mercy on them.
On that day the Lord will set a barrier from the channel of the River as far as the region of Rhinocorura. But you, gather the children of Israel one by one.

And on that day they will sound a great trumpet. Those scattered in the land of the Assyrians and those lost in the land of the Egyptians will come and worship the Lord on the holy mountain in Jerusalem.
Woe to that crown of pride of the hirelings of Ephraim, a flower fallen from its glory upon the summit of that fertile mountain—you who are drunk, but not with wine!

Look, the Lord’s fierce and severe anger comes down like hail, and there will be no shelter, and like the force of a flood of mighty waters that overwhelms the earth; he will give the earth rest with his hands.
And the crown of pride of those hired men of Ephraim will be trampled.
And the flower of hope, shaken loose from glory on the summit of the high mountain, will be like an early-ripe fig that someone sees and wants to swallow before taking it in hand.
On that day the Lord of hosts will be a crown of hope, made for the glory of the survivors of his people,
so that they may remain in a spirit of judgment, and through judgment and strength he will keep them from laziness.

For they have gone astray through wine; they went astray because of strong drink. The priest and the prophet became foolish because of strong drink; they were swallowed up by wine; they raved in their drunkenness from strong drink; they went astray, for that itself is foolishness.
Curses will consume that plan, because that plan comes from greed.
To whom shall we tell these evils? To whom shall we announce the bad news? To those taken off milk, to those weaned from the breast?
Afflictions upon afflictions; receive, receive; anxieties upon anxieties.
A little more, a little more. Because of the folly of their lips, they will speak to this people in foreign languages,
and they will say to them, “That is rest for the hungry, and this is destruction.” But they would not listen.

And the word of the Lord will be to them: “Afflictions upon afflictions; receive, receive; anxieties upon anxieties. A little more, a little more,” until they go and fall backward, and are broken, tormented, and destroyed.
Therefore hear the word of the Lord, you afflicted men and rulers of this people in Jerusalem,

because you say, “We have made a covenant with Hades and forged an alliance with death. If a raging storm arises, it will not come upon us, because we have made falsehood our hope and have covered ourselves with lies.”
Therefore the Lord God says: “Look, I am laying in the foundations of Zion a costly stone, a chosen, precious cornerstone in its foundations, and whoever believes in it shall not be put to shame.
And I will make justice a source of hope, and put my mercy in the balance. And those who have vainly trusted in falsehood say that the storm will not reach us,
and will not remove our covenant with death. Let your hope in Hades not stand firm, for if a raging storm comes, you will be trampled by it.”
For whenever it passes through, it will seize you. Morning after morning it will pass through, by day and by night, and there will be fear of calamities.
Learn to listen, you who are afflicted. We can no longer fight, because we have grown weak in our gathering, like the mountain of the wicked.

The Lord will arise in the valley of the Gibeonites, full of anger. He will do his work, a work of bitterness, so that his wrath will be judged in a strange way, and his bitterness will come in a strange way.
And do not rejoice, and do not let your bonds grow stronger, for I have heard from the Lord, the Lord of hosts, of settled and swift acts that he will carry out over all the earth.
Give ear and hear my voice; pay attention and hear my words.
Does the plowman plow all day, or does he sow the seed before the land has been worked?
Does he not first soften its surface and then sow a little black cumin and cumin, and then sow wheat, barley, millet, and spelt within their proper boundaries?
And you will be instructed in the ordinances of your God, and you will be glad.
For black cumin is not cleaned with a hard implement, nor is the wheel of a threshing cart driven over cumin. Instead, black cumin is beaten out with a staff, and cumin is eaten with bread.
For I will not be angry with you forever, nor will the sound of my bitterness trample you.
And these signs came forth from the Lord of hosts. Now consider: put away your empty consolation.
Woe to you, Ariel, city of Ariel, which David besieged! For the festivals will crowd together. Gather crops and eat year after year, and you will be consumed along with Moab.
For I will distress Ariel, and its strength and greatness will be mine.
And I will besiege you as David did, build a rampart against you, and erect towers around you.

Your words will be brought low to the earth, and your utterances will sink into the ground. Your voice will be like the voice of those who speak from the ground, and your voice will grow faint in the depths.
The vast host of the ungodly will be like dust from a wheel, and the multitude of your oppressors like sifted chaff. And it will happen in the blink of an eye.
From the Lord of hosts will come a visitation with an earthquake, thunder, and a mighty sound, a raging whirlwind, and a consuming flame of fire.
The vast host of all the nations attacking Jerusalem, all those gathered against it, and those who oppressed it will be like someone seeing a dream in a vision of the night.

They will be like those who are hungry in a dream and eat, but when they wake, the vision is empty; or like someone who is thirsty in a dream and drinks, but wakes and is thirsty again: his soul hoped in vain. So will it be with the vast host of all the nations that assembled their armies against Jerusalem and against Mount Zion.
Be astonished and become foolish; be dazed and become still more dazed, you who are drunk, but not from wine or strong drink.
For the Lord has made you drink a spirit of foolishness, and he will close your eyes and the eyes of your prophets, your rulers, and your seers.
All these utterances will be to you like the words of a sealed document. When they give it to a man who can read and say to him, “Read this,” he will say, “I cannot read it, because it is sealed.”
And the same document will be put into the hands of a man who cannot read, and they will say to him, “Read this.” And he will say, “I do not know how to read.”

And the Lord says, “This people draws near to me with its mouth, and they honor me with their lips, but their hearts are far removed from me. They worship me in vain, teaching human commandments and doctrines.”

“Therefore, look: I will once again transform this people. I will transform them, destroy the wisdom of the wise, and scorn the counsels of the counselors. Woe to those who devise deep plans, but not through the Lord!”
Woe to those who devise secret plans! Their deeds will be in darkness, and they will say, “Who will see us, and who will know what we are doing?”
Are you not regarded as a potter’s clay? Will the thing formed say to its maker, “You did not form me,” or the creature to its creator, “You did not make me with wisdom”?
Will it not be only a little while before Lebanon becomes like Mount Carmel, and Carmel is regarded as a forest?
On that day the deaf will hear the words of that book, and the eyes of the blind, who are in darkness and gloom, will see.
The poor will rejoice with gladness because of the Lord, and those among humankind who have no hope will be filled with joy.
The lawless one has come to an end, the arrogant one has perished, and those who act lawlessly in wickedness have been destroyed.
