They make people sin through words, set stumbling blocks for all who rebuke at the gates, and unjustly pervert justice.
Therefore, this is what the Lord says concerning the house of Jacob, whom he chose from Abraham: Jacob will no longer be ashamed, nor will Israel’s face now turn pale.
But when his children see my works, they will sanctify my name for my sake. They will sanctify the Holy One of Jacob and fear the God of Israel.
Those who are astray in spirit will come to know wisdom, and those who grumble will learn obedience, and stammering tongues will learn to speak peace.
Thus says the Lord: “Woe to you, rebellious children! For you devised a plan, but not through me, and you forge alliances, but not through my Spirit, adding sins to sins.”
who were going down to the land of the Egyptians without consulting me, to find help from Pharaoh and make the Egyptians your support.
Pharaoh’s support will become a shame to you, and those who trust in the Egyptians will suffer disgrace.
For in the land of Tanis there are rulers who are evil angels.
They labor in vain for a people who will bring them no benefit as a help or an advantage, but only shame and disgrace.

A vision of four-footed beasts in the wilderness: in distress and hardship are a lion and a lion’s cub, and among them vipers and flying offspring of vipers. They carry their treasures loaded on donkeys and their riches piled on camels to a nation that will offer them no benefit or help, but only shame and disgrace.
The Egyptians will help you in vain and to no purpose. Tell them, ‘This comfort of yours is in vain.’
Now sit down and write on a tablet and in a book, so that this may remain for its appointed day and for all time:
that this is a disobedient people, lying children who were unwilling to hear the law of God.
They said to the prophets, ‘Do not tell us these things. Instead, speak to us and tell us misleading things.
Turn us away from that road, remove that path from us, and take away from us the law of the God of Israel.’
Therefore the Lord, the Holy One of Israel, says this: ‘Because you despised these words and trusted in empty falsehood, and because you grumbled and trusted in that word,
therefore these sins will be to you like the suddenly collapsed wall of a strong city that has been captured, upon which destruction comes unexpectedly.’
Its destruction will be like the breaking of a potter’s earthen vessel, shattered into small pieces, so that no one will find a piece of it with which to take up fire or draw a little water.

For the Lord, the Lord, the Holy One of Israel, says this: ‘When you turn back and sigh, then you will live and know where you are. For you trusted in vain things, and your strength also became vain, and you were unwilling to listen.
Instead, you said, “We will flee on our horses.” Therefore you will become fugitives. And you will say, “We will flee on our swift horses.” Therefore those who pursue you will be swifter than you.
For at the voice of one, thousands will flee, and at the voice of five, many will flee, until you are left like a pole planted on a mountain and like a monument standing on a hill.’
And again God will hasten to have compassion on you, and therefore he will rise up to show you mercy, for the Lord our God is a judge. Blessed are all who wait for him.
For a holy people will dwell in Zion, and Jerusalem wept bitterly, saying, ‘Have mercy on me.’ He will have mercy on you at the sound of your cry, when he sees and hears you.
And the Lord will give you bread of distress and water of deprivation. Those who led you astray will no longer come near you, for your eyes will see those who lead you astray,
and your ears will hear words behind those who lead you astray, who said, ‘This is the road, and let us walk along it,’ whether to the right or to the left.
You will loathe the silver-plated and gold-plated idols. You will crush them and pour them out like menstrual fluid, and reject them like dung.
Then there will be rain for the seed sown in your land, and bread from the produce of your land will be plentiful and nourishing. On that day your flocks will graze in a rich pasture and in peace.
Your calves and oxen that work the land will eat straw mixed with barley, winnowed on the threshing floor.
And on every high mountain and every lofty hill there will be flowing water on that day, when many perish and towers collapse.

The light of the moon will be like the light of the sun, and the light of the sun will be seven times brighter, like the light of seven days, on the day when the Lord heals the brokenness of his people and heals the pain of your wounds.

Behold, the name of the Lord comes [?], after a long time, burning with anger. The words of his lips are full of glory, and the words of his mouth are full of anger, and his furious wrath will devour like fire.

And his spirit will surge like water filling a ravine, rising to the neck. It will divide to throw the nations into turmoil because of their vain delusion, and delusion will pursue them and come upon them face to face.
Must you always enter my holy places with joy, at every time with festivals and rejoicing, and enter the mountain of the Lord with trumpets, coming to God, the Holy One of Israel?

And he will make the glory of his voice heard and display the wrath of his arm, with anger and fury, with a devouring flame, with the fierce fury of fiery bolts, and with water and hail pouring down together violently.
For at the voice of the Lord the Assyrians will be crushed by the blows with which he strikes them.

And help will come to him from his helpers all around, from whatever direction he has placed his hope in. For they will fight against him in turn, with trumpets and a drum and various kinds of warfare, and you will not be called to account before those days.
But now, has it also been prepared for you to reign over the deep ravine, with wood piled up, fire, and a great heap of wood? The burning wrath of the Lord is like a ravine full of blazing sulfur.

Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help, who put their hope in horsemen and chariots because they are numerous, and in the very great number of horses, but did not put their hope in the Holy One of Israel and did not seek God.
And he was wise and brought disasters upon them, and his word will not be disregarded. He will rise against the houses of wicked people and against their vain hope.

In an Egyptian man, and not in God; in the flesh of horses, and there was no help. But the Lord will lay his hand upon them, and the helpers will suffer, and those helped by them will fall, and all together will perish.

For this is what the Lord said to me: As a lion and a lion's cub roar over the prey they come upon, crying out over it and filling the mountains with their voice, and they are defeated and melt away before the intensity of its wrath, so the Lord of hosts will descend upon Mount Zion and upon its mountains.
Like birds in flight, so the Lord of hosts will be a shelter over Jerusalem. He will descend to its aid, help it, rescue it, and preserve it alive.
Turn back, you who devise deep and lawless schemes, children of Israel.
For on that day people will cast away their handmade objects of silver and gold, which their hands made for sin.
And the Assyrian will fall, not by a man's sword, and no human sword will devour him. He will turn to flight, though not before a sword, and his young men will be defeated.

And the rock barriers will become like wall barriers, and they will be defeated, and whoever flees will be captured. This is what the Lord says: Blessed is the one who has offspring in Zion and whose household is in Jerusalem.
For behold, a righteous king will reign, and rulers will govern with justice.
And there will be a man who conceals his words; he will hide as though from the violence of waters. And Zion will be like a glorious, overflowing river in a thirsty land.
And they will no longer put their hope in people, but will give their ears to listen.
And the hearts of the weak will pay attention and listen, and stammering tongues will quickly learn to speak peace.
And they will no longer tell the fool to be their ruler, and your servants will no longer say, “Be silent.”
For the fool will speak foolishness, and his heart will devise worthless things: to commit lawlessness, to speak error against God, to scatter the hungry, and to send the thirsty away empty.
For the plans of the wicked devise lawless things: to destroy the lowly with unjust words and to dismiss the words of the needy in court.
But the upright have made wise plans, and that counsel stands and endures.
Wealthy women, rise and listen to my voice; anxious daughters, listen to my words.
Let the days of the year be remembered by you with pain and anxiety. The harvests have withered, the sowings have ceased, and they will not come again.
Tremble, you who live comfortably; grieve, you who trust in yourselves. Strip yourselves naked, remove your clothes, and put on sackcloth.
Beat your breasts in mourning for the desirable fields and the fruitful vineyards.
Thorns and grass will grow on the land of my people, and joy will be removed from every palace of your exalted city; the palaces are abandoned.
They will abandon the grandeur of your city and its desirable houses, and your towns will become caves forever, a delight for wild donkeys and pasture for flocks.
Until the Spirit comes upon you from on high, and the wilderness becomes Carmel, and Carmel is reckoned a forest.
And justice will rest in the wilderness, and righteousness will dwell in Carmel.
And the works of righteousness will be peaceful, and righteousness will maintain rest, and those who trust will endure forever.
And my people will dwell in the city of peace and live in hope, and they will rest in abundance.
But if hail falls, it will not come upon you, and those who dwell in the forest will be free from care, like those who are in the plain.
Blessed are those who sow beside every water, where the ox and donkey tread.

Woe to those who afflict you! Yet no one can afflict you, and the one who despises does not despise you. For those who despise you will be handed over to defeat, and like a moth upon rags, so they will be handed over to defeat.
Lord, have mercy on us, for we have trusted in you. The offspring of the unbelievers has come to ruin, but our salvation comes from you in a time of distress.
At the sound of your terror the peoples became senseless, and out of fear of you the nations scattered.
And now the plunder taken from you, both great and small, will be gathered as someone might gather locusts; as if from a pit, so they will mock you.
Holy is the Lord our God, who dwells on high. Zion has been filled with justice and righteousness.
They will be handed over according to the laws, and our salvation will be among treasures. Wisdom, understanding, and devotion to the Lord have come; these are the treasures of righteousness.
Look, those whom you feared will be afraid because of the terror you cause; they will fear you. They will send messengers who will weep bitterly and seek peace.
For their roads have been cut off, the terror of the nations has ceased, and the covenant with them has been removed. No longer count them as human beings.
The land mourned and grew weak; Lebanon was put to shame; Sharon was reckoned a meadow in the plain; Galilee and Carmel were laid bare.
Now I will arise, says the Lord; now I will be glorified; now I will be exalted.
Now you will see; now you will be put to shame. The strength of your spirits will be useless, and fire will devour you.
And the nations will be scorched like thorns in a field, burned and cast away.
Let those far away hear what I have done; let those nearby know my strength.
The lawless were driven out of Zion; trembling will seize the ungodly. Now who will tell you that a blazing fire is there, or who will tell you about the eternal dwelling place?

The one who walks in righteousness, speaks of the straight path, hates lawlessness and injustice, shakes his hands free of bribes, stops his ears from hearing a judgment of bloodshed, and closes his eyes so as not to see injustice—
He will dwell in a high cave in solid rock. Bread will be given to him, and his water will be assured.
You will see the King of glory, and your eyes will see the land from afar.

And your souls will meditate in the fear of the Lord. Where are the scribes? Where are the counselors? Where is the one who keeps the count of those receiving provisions, of the small and great among the people?
With whom he took no counsel, for he did not understand the one with the deep voice because he did not hear—a debased people, and the hearer has no understanding.
Behold Zion, the city of our salvation! Your eyes will see Jerusalem, a city grown great, tents that will not be moved. The stakes of its tent will never be moved, and its cords will not be broken.

For the name of the Lord is great among you. You will have a place where the rivers and waterways are broad and spacious. You will not travel along that route, nor will your rowed ships go there, for my God is great and will not pass me by.
The Lord is our father; the Lord is our judge; the Lord is our ruler; the Lord is our king; the Lord is our savior, and he will save us.
Your ropes have broken because they did not hold firm. Likewise, the mast has bent down, and it will not spread the sail or unfurl the flag until it is given over to destruction.
After this, many lame people will take plunder, and they will not say, “We have grown weary.” The people who dwell among them will have their sins forgiven.
Come near, nations, and hear! Pay attention, rulers! Let the earth hear, and all that is in it, the world and the peoples in it.
For the Lord's wrath is upon all nations, and his anger upon all their hosts, to destroy them and deliver them to slaughter.
And their wounded will fall dead, their stench will rise, and the mountains will be drenched with their blood.
And all the powers of heaven will melt, and the heavens will be rolled up like parchment. All the stars will fall like leaves from a vine and as leaves fall from a fig tree.
For my sword has become drunk in heaven. Now it will descend upon the Edomites and upon the people doomed to destruction, in judgment.
The Lord's sword is filled with blood and swollen with the fat of lambs and the fat of bulls and rams, for the Lord has a sacrifice in Bozrah and a great slaughter in the land of the Edomites.
The mighty will fall with them, along with rams and bulls. The land will be drunk with their blood, and their soil will be filled with their fat.
For it is the Lord's day of judgment and the year of recompense for Zion's judgment.
And its valleys will turn into pitch, and its land into sulfur, and its land will become like burning pitch,

By day and by night, and it will never be extinguished. Its smoke will rise upward, and it will be laid waste from generation to generation. For a long time it will lie desolate, and no one will pass through it.
Birds and hedgehogs, kites and ravens will dwell in it. Measuring lines of desolation will fall upon it, and ass-centaurs will dwell in it.
And its rulers will be as though they had never existed, and its kings and nobles will come to destruction.
And thorn-bearing trees will grow in its cities and fortresses, and it will become a dwelling place for sirens and a resting place for ostriches.
And demons will meet ass-centaurs and call to one another. There the ass-centaurs will rest, for they have found a resting place for themselves.
There the hedgehog brought forth its young, and the earth carefully nourished its young. There stags met one another and saw each other’s faces.
They passed by in number, and not one of them was missing. They did not seek one another, for the Lord commanded them, and his spirit gathered them.
He himself assigned them their portions by lot, and his hand divided pastures among them for all time. They will inherit them from generation to generation and rest there.
Rejoice, thirsty wilderness! Let the wilderness exult and blossom like a lily.
The wilderness of the Jordan will blossom and exult. The glory of Lebanon will be given to it, and the splendor of Carmel. My people will see the glory of the Lord and the majesty of our God.
Be strong, slack hands and buckling knees!
Take comfort, you who are fainthearted! Be strong and do not fear. Look, our God will repay with judgment, and he himself will give recompense. He will come and save you.
Then the eyes of the blind will be opened, and the ears of the deaf will hear.
Then the lame will leap like a deer, and the tongues of those who have difficulty speaking will become clear, for water has burst forth in the wilderness, and a river in the thirsty land.
The waterless land will become pools, and there will be a spring of water in the thirsty land. There will be joy for birds and resting places for flocks; there will be meadows and [?].

There will be a purified road there, and it will be called a holy road. No unclean person will pass along it, and there will be no road there for the unclean. But those who have been scattered will travel along it and will not go astray.
There will be no lion there, and none of the fierce beasts will pass along it or be found there at all. But the redeemed and those gathered for the Lord will travel along it.

They will return and come to Zion with rejoicing, and everlasting joy will be upon their heads, for a blessing will be upon their heads. Rejoicing and gladness will come to them; pain, sorrow, and sighing have been driven away.
In the fourteenth year of Hezekiah’s reign, Sennacherib king of the Assyrians came up against the fortified cities of Judah and captured them.
The king of the Assyrians sent Rabshakeh from Lachish to Jerusalem, to King Hezekiah, with a large army. He came and stood at the conduit of the upper pool, on the road to the fuller’s field.
Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was the chief steward, Shebna, the secretary for official correspondence, and Joah son of Asaph, the recorder, went out to him.
Rabshakeh said to them, “Go and tell Hezekiah: Thus says the great king of the Assyrians: In whom have you placed your trust?
Can a war be won by counsel or words spoken by the lips? In whom, then, have you placed your trust, that you refuse to submit to me?

Look, you have placed your trust in that broken reed of a staff, the Egyptian. If anyone leans on it, it breaks and pierces his hands. Such is Pharaoh king of the Egyptians, and all who place their trust in him.
But if you say, ‘We have placed our trust in the Lord our God,’ is he not the one whose high places and altars Hezekiah demolished, commanding Judah and Jerusalem to worship only before his altar?
Now, then, come and make an agreement with my lord, the king of the Assyrians, and I will give you two thousand horses, if you can provide riders for them.
How can you resist even one of the governors who serve my lord, when you rely on Egypt for its horsemen and horses?
Have we now come to this land to wage war against it without the Lord? The Lord said to me, ‘Go up against that land and destroy it.’”

Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah said to him, “Speak to your servants in Aramaic, for we understand it. Do not speak to us in Hebrew. Why should you speak within the hearing of the people who are resting on this wall?”

Rabshakeh said to them, “Did my lord send me to your master or to you to speak these words? Was it not to the people sitting on that wall, so that they will not eat dung and drink their own urine along with you?”
Rabshakeh stood up and cried out in a loud voice in Hebrew, saying, “Hear the words of the great king, the king of the Assyrians!”
This is what the king says: Do not let Hezekiah deceive you with words by which he cannot save you.
And do not let Hezekiah mislead you by saying, ‘God will save you, and this city will not be handed over to the king of Assyria.’

Do not listen to Hezekiah. This is what the king of Assyria says: If you wish to make things easier for yourselves, come out to me. Then each of you will eat from his own vineyard and fig tree and drink water from your own wells,
until I come and take you to a land like your own land, a land of wheat and wine, plentiful in bread and vineyards.
Do not let Hezekiah deceive you by saying, ‘God will save you.’ Did the gods of the nations save their respective lands from the hand of the king of Assyria?
Where is the god of Hamath and Arpad, and where is the god of the city of Sepharvaim? Were they able to save Samaria from my hands?
Which of the gods of all those nations was able to save his land from my hands, that your God should save Jerusalem from my hands?
They remained silent and gave no answer, because the king had commanded them not to answer.

Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was the chief steward, Shebna, the secretary for royal correspondence, and Joah son of Asaph, the recorder, came to Hezekiah with their garments torn at the neck and told him the words of the Rabshakeh.
When King Hezekiah heard this, he tore his robe, put on sackcloth, and went up to the house of the Lord.
He sent Eliakim the chief steward, Shebna the secretary for royal correspondence, and the elders of the priests, dressed in sackcloth, to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.
They said to him: This is what Hezekiah says: Today is a day of distress, disgrace, rebuke, and wrath, a day when the pains of childbirth have come upon a woman in labor, but she cannot give birth.

May the Lord your God hear the words of the Rabshakeh, whom his master, the king of Assyria, sent to insult the living God and to insult him with words that the Lord your God has heard. Now petition the Lord your God for these who remain.
The servants of King Hezekiah came to Isaiah.
Isaiah said to them, “Tell your master this: Thus says the Lord: Do not be afraid of the words you have heard, with which the messengers of the king of Assyria have insulted me.”
Look, I will put a spirit of unrest within him. When he hears a report, he will return to his own country and fall by the sword in his own land.
The Rabshakeh returned and reached the king of Assyria, for he was besieging Libnah, and he heard that the king of Assyria had departed from Lachish.
Tirhakah, king of the Ethiopians, came out to besiege him, and he returned. He sent messengers to Hezekiah and said:
Say this to Hezekiah king of Judah: “Do not let your God, in whom you trust, deceive you by saying, ‘Jerusalem will not be delivered into the hands of the king of Assyria.’”
Now, have you not heard what the kings of Assyria did to every land, how they destroyed them? Will you, then, escape?
Did the gods of the nations save those whom my fathers destroyed—Gozan, Haran, and Rezeph, which are in the land of Hamath?
Where are the kings of Hamath and Arpad, and where are the kings of the city of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah?
Hezekiah took the letter from the hands of the messengers and read it. He entered the house of the Lord and spread it out before the Lord.
Hezekiah began to pray to the Lord and said:
Lord of hosts, God of Israel, enthroned upon the cherubim, you alone are God over all the kingdoms of the world. You made heaven and earth.
Incline your ear, Lord, and hear. Open your eyes, Lord, and look. Lord, hear; Lord, see the messages that Sennacherib, king of Assyria, sent to insult the living God.
Indeed, the kings of Assyria have laid waste all the countries and their lands.
And they burned their idols, for they were not gods but the work of human hands, made of wood and stone, and they destroyed them.
But now, Lord our God, save us from his hand, so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you alone are God.
And Isaiah son of Amoz was sent to Hezekiah and said to him, “This is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says: I have heard the prayer you offered to me concerning Sennacherib, king of Assyria.
Now this is the word God spoke concerning him: The virgin daughter of Zion despised you and scorned you; the daughter of Jerusalem shook her head at you.
Whom have you insulted and provoked? Against whom have you raised your voice? And have you not lifted your eyes on high against the Holy One of Israel?

Why have you insulted the Lord through your messengers? You said, ‘With my many chariots I climbed to the heights of the mountains and the far reaches of Lebanon. I cut down its tall cedars and its beautiful cypresses, and I entered the heights of the forest’s farthest regions.
And I laid a bridge and laid waste the waters and all the pools of water.’
Have you not heard what I did long ago, what I ordained in ancient days? Now I have revealed it: to lay waste the nations in their strongholds.
And I abandoned the inhabitants of the cities in their respective fortresses, and they dried up and became like withered grass on rooftops and like dried couch grass.
Now I myself know the places where you rest, and your going out and coming in along your roads.
And your rage, with which you raged, and your bitterness came before me. I will put a halter in your nose and a bridle on your jaws, and I will turn you back along the same road by which you came.
But this will be a sign for you: This year you will eat what has been sown, and next year you will eat what remains. In the third year you will sow and reap, plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
And the remnant of Judea will send roots downward and bear fruit upward.
For there will be a remnant in Jerusalem and survivors on Mount Zion, because the zeal of the Lord of hosts has done this.
Therefore this is what the Lord says concerning the king of Assyria: He must not enter this city or shoot arrows against it, surround it with shields or besiege it with siegeworks.
Instead, he will return by the same road by which he came, and he must not enter that city. This is what the Lord says.
I will watch over that city to save it, for my own sake and for the sake of David my servant.”
And the angel of the Lord went out and killed one hundred and eighty-five thousand in the Assyrian camp. When they rose in the morning, they found all those bodies dead.
And Sennacherib, king of Assyria, turned back and went away, and lived in Nineveh.
While he was worshiping in the temple of his idol Nisroch, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer killed him with the sword. They fled to Armenia, and his son Esarhaddon reigned in his place.

And at that time Hezekiah became mortally ill. Isaiah son of Amoz came to him and said to him, “This is what the Lord says: Give instructions concerning your household, for you will die and will not live.”
And Hezekiah turned his face toward the wall and began to pray.
He said, “O Lord, remember me, Lord, for I walked before you in righteousness and truth of heart, and I did what was pleasing before you.” And Hezekiah wept bitterly.
And the word of the Lord came to Isaiah, saying:
“Go and tell Hezekiah: This is what the Lord, the God of David your father, says: I have heard the sound of your prayers and seen your tears. Look, I am adding fifteen years to your life.
And I will save you and that city from the hand of the king of Assyria, and I will watch over that city.”
And this will be a sign to you from the Lord that God will fulfill this word that he spoke.

Look, I am turning back the shadow on these steps, down which the sunlight has descended ten steps in your house, and I will turn the sunlight back ten steps. And the sunlight went up ten steps by which the shadow had descended.
The prayer of Hezekiah, king of Judah, when he became ill and recovered from his illness.
I said, “As my days come to an end, I will go to the gates of Hades; I will leave behind the remainder of my years.”
I said, “I will no longer see God's salvation on earth, nor will I again see man among his fellow inhabitants.”

I was cut off from my family; I left behind the remainder of my life. They went out and departed from me, like someone who takes down a pitched tent. My spirit within me became like a web [?] about to be cut.
On that day I was given over until morning. Like a lion, he crushed all my bones, for from day until night I was given over.
I cried out like a swallow and moaned like a dove, for my eyes grew weak from looking toward the heights of heaven, toward the Lord who saved me and relieved the pain of my soul.
And he himself appointed all my years in bitterness of soul.
Lord, this was told to you, and you awakened my spirit. I was comforted and lived.
Look, my bitterness turned to peace. You saved my soul so that I would not perish, and you cast all my sins behind me.
For those who are in Hades will not give thanks to you, nor will the dead praise you, nor will those who descend into the pit hope in your mercy.
But the living will praise you, as I do. From now on I will father children who will recount your righteousness, Lord of my salvation.
And I will not cease to praise you with a harp all the days of my life before your temple, O God.
And Isaiah said to Hezekiah, “Take a cake of figs, crush it, and put it on your wound, and you will recover.”
And he said, “This will be a sign that I will go up to the house of God.”
At that time Merodach-baladan son of Baladan, king of the Babylonians, sent messengers with letters and gifts to Hezekiah, because he heard that he had been ill, near death, and had recovered.

Hezekiah was glad to receive them and showed them the storehouses of his treasures, incense, oils, gold, and silver, and all the storehouses of valuable vessels, and everything that was in his treasuries. There was nothing in his house or in all his dominion that Hezekiah did not show them.

And Isaiah the prophet came to King Hezekiah and said to him, “What do these men say, and where have they come from to you?” Hezekiah said, “They have come to me from a distant country, from Babylon.”
And Isaiah said, “What did they see in your house?” Hezekiah said, “They saw everything that was in my house. There was nothing in my house that they did not see, including my treasures.”
Isaiah said to him, “Now hear the words of the Lord of hosts.”

“Look, days will come when they will take everything that is in your house, and everything your ancestors have gathered up to this day, and carry it to Babylon. They will leave absolutely nothing.” But God said that:
And they will take some of your sons who will come from you, whom you will father, and make them eunuchs in the house of the king of the Babylonians.
And Hezekiah said to Isaiah, “The word of the Lord that he spoke is good. Let there be righteousness and peace in my days.”
“You priests, comfort, comfort my people,” says God.
Speak to the heart of Jerusalem and comfort her, for she has had her fill of suffering. Let her sins be forgiven, for she has received from the Lord's hand double repayment for her sins.
The voice of one crying in the wilderness: “Prepare the ways of the Lord, and make straight the paths of our God.”
Every valley will be filled, and every mountain and hill will be brought low; all difficult places will become easy to pass through, and rocky places will become plains.
The glory of the Lord will be revealed, and all flesh will see the salvation of God, for the Lord has spoken.
A voice says, “Cry out!” And I say, “What shall I cry out?” “Cry out: All flesh is grass, and all human glory is like the flower of grass.”
The grass withered, and its flower fell, because the Spirit of the Lord breathed upon it. Truly, this people is grass.
The grass withered and the flower fell, but the word of the Lord remains forever.

Go up onto a high mountain, you who bring good news to Zion. Raise your voice with strength, you who bring good news to Jerusalem. Raise it; do not be afraid. Say to the cities of Judah, “Here is your God!”
Look, the Lord God comes with power, and his arm with its own dominion. Look, his reward is with him, and his works are before him.
Like a shepherd, he will tend his flocks, and with his arm he will gather the lambs and carry them in his bosom, and he will comfort those that are pregnant.
Who measured the waters with his palm, and the heavens with a span, and all the earth with a handful? Who weighed the mountains on a scale and the plains with weights?
Who knew the mind of the Lord, and who became his counselor to give him understanding?
Or with whom did he consult, who gave him understanding? Or who showed him justice and the way of wisdom? Or who first lent him anything, so that he should repay it?
For all the nations are like a single drop from a bucket, and they were reckoned as a tiny weight on the scales, and they will be reckoned as drops from the mouth.
For Lebanon is not sufficient for burning, and all its four-footed animals are not sufficient for burnt offerings.
And all the nations are nothing, and they were reckoned as nothing before him.
Then to whom will you compare the Lord, and to whose likeness will you liken him?
Did a craftsman hammer him into an image? Or did a goldsmith cast gold and cover him with gold, shaping him into the likeness of an image?
The craftsman chose wood that would not rot, and skillfully seeks a way to set it up so that it will not move.
Do you not hear, and do you not understand? Was it not told to you from the beginning? Do you not know who established the foundations of the earth?
He holds the circle of the earth, and its inhabitants are like locusts. He set up the heavens like a vault and stretched them out like a tent, and established the earth to be inhabited.
He reduces the rulers' authority to nothing and made the earth as nothing.
For they will not sow or plant, nor will their root become established in the earth. He breathed upon them, and they withered, and a storm will carry them away like dry brushwood.
“Then to whom will you compare me, so that I should be his equal?” says the Holy One of Israel.
Lift your eyes on high and see who established all these things, who brings out their array and calls them all by name, with great glory and mighty strength; not one thing was hidden from you.
Do not say this, Jacob; and why have you said, Israel, “My ways were hidden from God, and my God took away my rights”?

And they departed [?]. And now, did you not know, or had you not heard? God is eternal, the God who established the ends of the earth. He will neither hunger nor grow weary, and his wisdom cannot be fathomed.
He gives strength to the hungry and sorrow to those without pain.
Young men will hunger, and youths will grow weary, and the chosen will become powerless.
But those who wait for the Lord will be renewed in strength; they will be adorned with new feathers like eagles. They will run and not grow weary; they will walk and not hunger.
Renew yourselves before me, islands, so that rulers may be renewed in strength. Let them approach and speak together, and then let them state their case.

Who raised up righteousness from the east and called him to follow him? He will bring retribution before the nations and terrify kings. He will turn their swords to dust and drive away their arrows like chaff.
And he will put them to flight and travel peacefully along the paths of his feet.
Will you now say that he will not come? Who announced and did all this? He who called from the earliest generations called him. I am the Lord, the first, and I am the same hereafter.
The nations saw me and were afraid, and all the ends of the earth trembled. They approached and came together.
Each resolved to help his neighbor and his brother, and they will say:

The carpenter will encourage the smith to forge, beat, and strike with the hammer, and he will say, “This has been a good help to me.” And they fastened them with nails and will set them on the ground, and they will not move.
But you, Israel, are my servant, Jacob whom I chose, the offspring of Abraham whom I loved.
For whom I became a helper from the ends of the earth. From its watchtowers I called you and said, “You are my servant.” I chose you and will not abandon you.
Do not be afraid, for I am with you. Do not be deceived, for I am your God, who strengthened you, helped you, and guarded you with my righteous right hand.
Look, all your adversaries will be ashamed and disgraced. They will become as though they had never existed, and all who bring charges against you will perish.
You will seek them but will not find the people who treated you with hostility, and those who wage war against you will become as though they had never existed.
For I am the Lord your God, who holds your right hand and says to you, “Do not be afraid; I will help you.”
Do not be afraid, you worm of Jacob, you [?] of Israel. I have helped you, says God, who will redeem you, the Holy One of Israel.
Look, I will make you like the new, saw-toothed wheels of threshing carts. You will crush the mountains and pulverize the hills and make them like dust.
You will winnow them; winds will carry them away, and storms will scatter them. But you will rejoice in the Lord, in the holy things of Israel.

And the poor and needy will rejoice, those who sought water and could not find it, whose tongues were drying up from thirst. I, the Lord God, the God of Israel, will hear them and will not abandon them.
Instead, I will open rivers upon the mountains and springs in the midst of the plains. I will turn the wilderness into pools of water and the thirsty land into streams.
And I will cause the cedar, boxwood, myrtle, cypress, plane tree, [?], [?], poplar, juniper, and olive tree to spring up in the waterless land.
So that they may see and know, recognize and understand together that the Lord’s hand did all this, and the Holy One of Israel established it.
Your cases have drawn near, says the Lord God. Your cases have drawn near, says the King of Jacob.
Let them approach and tell you what events are going to happen. Or tell us what the former things were, so that we may consider them and know what came first and what comes afterward.
Tell us, report to us what will happen in the end, so that we may know whether you are gods. Do good; do evil, so that we may see together and be amazed.
Where are you from, and where is your work from? For they chose you, abominations, from the earth.
But I will raise up the one from the north and the one from the east; they will be called by my name. Princes will come, and you will trample them like potter’s clay that the potter treads.

Who will tell what has been from the beginning, so that we may know, and what happened still earlier, so that we may say, “It is true”? There is no one who speaks beforehand, nor anyone who hears your words.
I will give Zion a beginning, and I will comfort Jerusalem along the way.
For look, there is no one among the nations, and no one among their idols, who tells anything. Even if I ask them, “Where are you from?” they will give me no answer.
For those who make you are empty, and those who fashion you are worthless.
Jacob is my servant; I will be his helper. Israel is my chosen one, whom my soul has accepted. I have put my Spirit upon him, and he will bring forth justice for the nations.
He will not cry out or quarrel, and no one will hear his voice outside.
He will not break a bruised reed or extinguish a smoldering wick, but he will bring forth justice in truth.
He will shine forth and will not be crushed until he establishes justice on earth, and the nations will hope in his name.
Thus says the Lord God, who made the heavens and set them in place, who established the earth and what is in it, who gave breath to the people upon it and spirit to all who walk on it:
I, the Lord God, called you in righteousness, took hold of your right hand, strengthened you, and gave you as a covenant for the people and as a light for the nations,
to open the eyes of the blind, to bring prisoners out of prison, and those who sat in darkness out of the house of confinement.
I am the Lord God; this is my name. I will not give my glory to another, nor my praise to carved images.
What was there from the beginning has come to pass. I will tell you new things, and before they were told, they were shown to you [?].
Praise the Lord with new praise, for his dominion is glorified in the heights, and his name from the ends of the earth—you who go down to the sea in ships, the islands and their inhabitants.
Let the wilderness and its towns rejoice, the camps and inhabitants of Kedar. Let the inhabitants of the Rock rejoice; let them shout from the mountaintops.
Let them give glory to God, and let the islands proclaim his might.
The Lord God of hosts will come and wage war. He will stir up his zeal and shout mightily against his enemies.
I have been silent from the beginning. Will I always remain silent and listen? I have endured like a woman giving birth. Now I will terrify and dry up everything at once.
I will lay low the mountains and hills and dry up all their grass. I will turn rivers into islands and dry up the [?].

I will lead the blind along a road they do not know, and make them walk along paths they did not recognize. I will turn darkness into light for them and difficult ways into easy ones. I will do these things for them and will not abandon them.
But they turned back from me. Be greatly ashamed, you who trust in carved images and say to cast images, ‘You are our gods.’
You who are deaf, listen; you who are blind, look so that you may see.
Who is blind if not my servant, and who are deaf if not those who rule over them? Who is blind if not the one who has gone away? And the servants of God became blind.
Look many times, yet you have not paid attention. Your eyes were open, yet you did not hear.
The Lord God wished to be justified and to exalt praise.

And I saw that the people had been plundered and handed over as spoil, with snares in all the storehouses and in all the palaces alike, where they hid them. They became plunder, and there was no one to rescue them; they became spoil, and there was no one to say, ‘Bring them out.’
Who among you will listen to all this and take to heart what is to come afterward?
Who gave Jacob over to plunder and Israel to looters? Was it not God, against whom they sinned? They would not walk in his ways or listen to his laws.
He brought the fury of his anger upon him, and war surrounded them. There were fire-setters all around them, yet none of them understood or took it to heart.
And now, thus says the Lord God, who made you, Jacob, and who formed you, Israel: Do not be afraid, for I have redeemed you and called you by your name, saying, ‘You are mine.’
And if you pass through the waters, I am with you, and the rivers shall not overwhelm you. And if you pass through fire, you shall not be burned, and its flame shall not scorch you.
For I am the Lord your God, the Holy One of Israel, who saves you. I gave Egypt in exchange for you, and I exchanged Ethiopia and Syene for you.
Because you became precious in my sight and were honored, and I loved you, I will give people in exchange for you and rulers in exchange for your life.
Do not be afraid, for I am with you. I will bring your offspring from the east and gather you from the west,
I will say to the north, “Bring them,” and to the south, “Do not hold them back. Bring my sons from a distant land and my daughters from the ends of the earth.”
and everyone who is called by my name, for I established him by my glory, and created him, and made him.
And I brought out the blind people, who, although they have eyes, are nevertheless blind, and their ears are stopped.

All the nations gathered together, and the rulers shall assemble. Who among them will declare this? Or who will make known to you what was from the beginning? Let them bring their witnesses and be justified; let them hear and speak the truth.

Be my witnesses, and I am a witness for you, says the Lord God, and my servant whom I chose, so that you may know and believe me and understand that I am. Before me no other God came into being, and after me there shall be none.
I am God, and there is no one besides me who can save.
I declared, and saved, and reproached, and there was no stranger among you. You yourselves bear witness to me.
And I am the Lord God from the beginning and still, and there is no one who can deliver from my hands. I will act, and there is no one who can reverse it.
Thus says the Lord God, who will redeem you, the Holy One of Israel: For your sake I sent to Babylon and drove them all out as fugitives, and the Chaldeans shall be besieged in ships.
I am the Lord God, your Holy One, who revealed to you the king of Israel.
Thus says the Lord, who made a way through the sea and paths through mighty waters,
who brings out chariots and horses and many mighty forces. But they lay down and shall not rise; they were extinguished like an extinguished wick.
Do not remember the former things, and do not call the ancient things to mind,
for behold, I am doing something new, which will now appear, and you shall know it. I will make a way through the wilderness and cause rivers to spring forth in a waterless land.
The beasts of the wilderness, sirens and ostriches, shall praise me, for I gave water in the wilderness and a river in a waterless land, to give drink to my chosen nation
and to my people, whom I acquired to declare my mighty deeds.
It was not just now that I called you, Jacob, nor did I make you toil, Israel.

You did not bring me sheep for your burnt offerings, nor did you glorify me with your sacrifices. You did not serve me with your offerings, and I did not make you toil over the expense of your frankincense.
You did not buy incense for me with silver, and I did not desire the fat of your sacrifices. But I will watch over you in your sins and your lawless deeds.
I, I am the one who blots out your lawless deeds for my own sake, and I will no longer remember your sins.
But remember, and let us plead our cases together. You first declare your lawless deeds, so that you may be justified.
Your fathers sinned first, and your rulers acted lawlessly against me.
And the rulers defiled my holy things, and I handed Jacob over to destruction and Israel to disgrace.
But now listen, Jacob my servant, and Israel, whom I chose.
Thus says the Lord God, who made you and formed you from the womb—and you will still find help: Do not be afraid, Jacob my servant, and my beloved Israel, whom I chose.
For I will give water to the thirsty who walk in a waterless land. I will place my Spirit upon your offspring and my blessings upon your children.
They will flourish like well-watered grass and like a willow among flowing waters.
One will say, “I belong to God,” and another will call out in the name of the God of Jacob. Another will write with his own hand, “I belong to God,” and will call out in the name of Israel.
Thus says God, the King of Israel, and God of hosts, who redeemed him: I am the first and I am the last; apart from me there is no other God.
Who is like me? Let him come forward, speak, declare it, and present himself before me, since I made humanity for eternity. Let them tell you what is to come before it comes.
Do not be astonished and do not be ashamed. Did you not hear from the beginning, and did I not tell you? You yourselves bear witness for me: Is there any other God besides me?

At that very time, all those who fashioned and carved worthless things were nothing. They made them according to their own desires, but these things will not help them. You are their witnesses, for they neither see nor understand.
Let the one who fashions an image and casts a carved idol to no purpose be ashamed.

And let all who associate with him also be ashamed—all who make idols and carve useless things. All those from whom they came have withered, deaf among people. Let them all gather and stand forth together; let them be ashamed and disgraced together.

For the carpenter bent his tool, sharpened an adze, and hammered with it. He worked with a chisel and fashioned it, and set it upright by the strength of his arm. He will grow hungry and weak, and he will drink no water.

The carpenter chose wood, measured it, and carved it into the likeness of an image. He shaped it with a chisel, joined it with glue, and made it in the form of a man, with the beautiful appearance of a human face. He set it up in his house.
This was the wood he cut down—the cypress or the plane tree, the oak or the elm—which the Lord planted and the rain made grow.

It was to be fuel for people. He took some of it, burned it, and warmed himself. With half of it he made bread, and the other half he made into an image, and he bowed down to them. He falls before the image he made for himself and worships it.
He burned half of it in a fire, baked bread over its coals, and roasted meat. He ate and was satisfied, and warmed himself, and says, “Ah, I have warmed myself and seen the fire!”
The other half he made into a carved god. He bowed down and worshiped it, stands in prayer before it, and says, “Save me, for you are my god.”
They did not take thought to understand, for they were blinded from seeing with their eyes and understanding with their hearts.

They did not consider or understand in their thoughts that they burned half the wood in the fire, made bread over its coals, roasted meat and ate it, and made the other half into an image and worship it.
Know that their heart is ashes, and they have gone astray. None of them can save their own lives. Look, yet you do not say, “There is deception in your hands.”
Remember these things, Jacob and Israel, for you are my servant. I created you to serve me. Israel, do not forget me.
For behold, I have wiped away your lawless deeds like a cloud and your sins like mist. Return to me, and I will redeem you.

Rejoice, heavens, for God has had mercy on Israel. Sound the trumpet, foundations of the earth. Shout for joy, mountains, hills, and all the trees in them, for God has redeemed Jacob, and Israel will be glorified.
Thus says the Lord, who redeemed you and formed you from the womb: I am the Lord who makes and completes everything. I stretched out the heavens alone and established the earth.
Who else scattered the signs of sorcerers and the desires from their hearts? Who turns the wise backward and makes their counsels foolish,

and confirms the words of his servants and vindicates the counsels of his messengers? I am the one who says to Jerusalem, “You will be inhabited,” and to the cities of Judea, “You will be rebuilt,” and I will raise up her ruins.
I am the one who says to the depths, “You will be laid waste,” and I will dry up her rivers.
who say to Cyrus, “Be wise and carry out all my wishes,” who say to Jerusalem, “Be built,” and I will establish my holy temple.

Thus says the Lord God to my anointed, Cyrus, whose right hand I have grasped to subdue nations before him: I will shatter the strength of kings and open doors before him, and cities will not be shut.
I will go before you and level the mountains. I will shatter bronze doors and break iron bars.
I will give you treasures hidden in darkness and reveal unseen stores to you, so that you may know that I am the Lord God, who called you by name, the God of Israel.
For the sake of Jacob my servant and Israel my chosen one, I will call you by your name and accept you.
Yet you did not know me—that I am the Lord God, and there is no one else.
And they will know from the east and from the west that there is no one besides me.
I am the one who established light and made darkness. I am the one who makes peace and establishes evil. I am the Lord God who does all these things.

Let the heavens above rejoice, and let the clouds drip righteousness. Let the earth pour forth mercy, and let it pour forth righteousness as well. I am the Lord who established you. I formed you as something good, like a potter’s clay.

Does the one who plows the earth plow all day? Will the clay say to the potter, “Why are you standing there? Why do you not work? You have no hands”? Will what was formed say to its maker, “Why did you form me this way?”
Woe to the one who says to his father, “Why did you beget me?” and to his mother, “Why did you suffer labor pains for me?”
For thus says the Lord God, the Holy One of Israel, who made the things that are to come: Ask me about my sons and daughters, and give me commands concerning the works of my hands.
I made the earth and humanity upon it. With my own hand I established the heavens. I gave commands to all the stars.
I raised him up as king in righteousness, and all his ways are straight. He will build my city and bring back my captive people, not for bribes or gifts, says the Lord of hosts.

Thus says the Lord of hosts: The land of the Egyptians has labored, and the merchandise of the Ethiopians and the Sabeans, men of great stature, will come over to you. They will serve you and walk behind you, bound with shackles. They will come to you and bow down to you and make a covenant with you, because God is in you. And they will say, “There is no other God besides you.”
For you are God, and we did not know it, the God of Israel, the Savior.
All his adversaries will be ashamed and disgraced, and they will depart in shame.
Renew yourselves before me, islands, for Israel has been saved with an everlasting salvation. They will not be ashamed or ever again be disgraced, forever.

For thus says the Lord, who made the heavens, the God who established the earth and made it: He is the one who set it in order. He did not make it in vain, but formed it to be inhabited. I am the Lord, and there is no one else.
I did not speak in secret or in a dark place of the earth. I did not say to Jacob’s descendants, “Seek vain things.” I am, I am the Lord, who speaks righteousness and declares truth.
Gather and come; take counsel together, you who have escaped from the nations. Those who carried carved wooden images and prayed to gods that could not save them did not understand.

If they can tell it, let them come near, then, so that they may know together. Who made all these things known from the beginning? From that time onward it was announced to you: I am God, and there is no one else besides me, righteous and a savior; there is no one besides me.
Turn to me and be saved, you who have come from the ends of the earth. I am God, and there is no one else.
I swear by myself that whatever comes out of my mouth is righteousness, and my words shall not be annulled: every knee shall bend to me, and every tongue shall acknowledge God.
And he will say, “Righteousness and glory will come to him,” and all who separate themselves from the Lord will be ashamed.
They will be justified, and all the offspring of the children of Israel will be glorified in God.
Bel has fallen; Dagon has been shattered. Their carved images have been placed on beasts and livestock. Carry them bound like a burden for the weary and hungry,
the exhausted and needy together, who could not escape from war; and they were led into captivity.
Listen to me, house of Jacob and all you who remain of Israel, chosen from the womb and instructed from childhood until old age,
that I am he; and even when you grow very old, I am still he. I bear with you. I made you, and I will heed you. I will receive you and save you.
To whom will you liken me? Look and think it over, you who have gone astray.
You pour out gold from a purse and weigh silver on scales, and you hire goldsmiths to make handmade idols, and you bow down and worship them.

You lift them and carry them on your shoulders. If you set one on the ground, it remains there in its place and does not move. If someone calls to it, it does not hear and will not save him from troubles.
Remember this and sigh. Repent, you who have gone astray; turn back with your hearts, and
Remember the former deeds from ages past, for I am God, and there is no one else besides me.
who declares the last things beforehand, before they have happened and are all accomplished. And I said, “All my plans will stand firm, and I will do everything I desire.”
calling birds from the east and from a distant land for what I planned. I spoke and brought it about; I established it and made it. I brought him and made his paths prosper.
Listen to me, you who are lost in heart, you who are far from righteousness.
I have brought my righteousness near, and it will no longer be far away. I will not delay my truth and my salvation. I have granted salvation in Zion for the glory of Israel.

Come down and sit on the earth, virgin daughter of Babylon. Sit on the ground, for there is no throne. Enter the darkness, daughter of the Chaldeans, and you will no longer be called delicate and tender.
Take a millstone and grind flour. Throw off your veil, pull back your hair, uncover your legs, and cross the rivers.
Your shame will be exposed, and your disgrace will be seen, for I will take your rights away from you. He will no longer hand you over to men.
The one who redeemed you—the Lord of hosts is his name, the Holy One of Israel.
Sit grieving and repentant; enter the darkness, daughter of the Chaldeans. You will no longer be called the power of kings.
I was angry with my people because they defiled my inheritance. I handed them over to you, and you showed them no mercy. You made the yoke on the elderly exceedingly heavy.
And you said, “I will remain a ruler forever.” You never took this to heart and did not remember the end.
Now hear this, you delicate one, who sat in self-confidence and said in your heart, “I am, and there is no one equal to me. I will not sit in widowhood, and I will not know orphanhood.”
Now both these things will come upon you suddenly in a single day: widowhood and childlessness will come upon you suddenly because of your divinations and your powerful sorceries.

And because of your confidence in your wicked deeds, for you said, “I am, and there is no one beside me,” know this and take it to heart: your prostitution will bring you shame, because you said in your heart, “I am, and there is no one beside me.”

Destruction will come upon you, which you will not understand, and a pit, and you will fall into it. Misery will come upon you, and you will not be able to cleanse yourself. Destruction will come upon you suddenly, and you will not recognize it.
Come now, persist in your divinations and your many sorceries, which you learned from your childhood. Can you gain any benefit? Can you regain strength?
For you have wearied yourself with your counsels. Let the astrologers who observe the stars of heaven rise up and save you; let them tell you what is going to come upon you.
Look, they will all burn in the fire like stubble, and let them not save themselves from the flame. For you sit upon fiery embers; let them be your helpers.
Your merchants labored in your trade from their childhood. One by one they went astray, and there will be no salvation for you.

Hear this, house of Jacob, you who are called by the name of Israel, who were born from the offspring of Judah, who swear by the name of the Lord God of Israel and invoke him, but not in truth or righteousness.
You take courage in the name of the holy city and consider yourselves firmly established in the name of the God of Israel. The Lord of Hosts is his name.
I announce the former things beforehand; they came from my mouth and were made known. Suddenly I acted, and they came to pass.
I know that you are stubborn, that the sinews of your neck are iron and your forehead is bronze.

The former things were announced to you, and before they reached you, I made them known to you, lest you ever say, “My idols did them,” or say, “My carved images and cast images announced them to me.”
Hear everything, yet you do not take it to heart. I have also made known to you the new things that will happen from now on.
And you did not say, “It happens now, and not long ago, in former days.” Nor did you hear of it, lest you say, “Yes, I know that.”
For you do not know or understand, and you have not opened your ears from the beginning. For I knew that you would act with utter contempt and would be called lawless from the womb.
For the sake of my name, I will show you my anger and my glory, which I have brought upon you, so that I may not destroy you.
Look, I sold you, but not for silver, and I delivered you from the furnace of poverty.
For my own sake I did this to you, so that my name might not be blasphemed, and I will not give my glory to another.
Listen to me, Jacob, and Israel, whom I call. I am the first, and I am forever.
My hand laid the foundations of the earth, and my right hand established the heavens. I will call them all, and they will stand together.
Let them all gather and hear: who announced this to them? Out of love for you, I carried out your will against Babylon, to remove the offspring of the Chaldeans.
I called, and I spoke. I brought him, and I made his ways prosper.
Come to me and hear this: from the beginning I have spoken nothing in secret, nor in a dark place of the earth. When it came into being, I was there. And now the Lord God has sent me, and his Spirit.
Thus says the Lord who redeemed you, the Holy One of Israel: “I am the Lord your God. I showed you how to find the path on which you should walk.”
If you had listened to my commandments, your peace would have been like a river, and your righteousness like the waves of the sea.
Your offspring would have been like the sand, and the children of your womb like the dust of the earth. Nevertheless, even now you will not be destroyed, nor will your name perish before me.
Leave Babylon; flee from the Chaldeans. Announce it with a joyful voice, and let it be heard. Proclaim to the ends of the earth, saying, “The Lord has redeemed his servant Jacob.”
And if they thirst in the wilderness, he will bring them water from a rock. The rock will split, waters will gush out, and my people will drink.
“There is no peace for the wicked,” says the Lord.
Listen to me, islands, and pay attention, nations. After a long time this will be established, says the Lord. He called me from the womb, and from my mother’s womb he called my name.
He made my mouth like a sharp sword and hid me under the shelter of his hand. He made me like a choice arrow and hid me in his quiver.
And he said to me, “You are my servant, Israel, and in you I will be glorified.”
And I said, “Then I have labored in vain; I have spent my strength uselessly, for nothing. Yet my justice comes from the Lord, and my labor is before my God.”
And now, thus says the Lord, who formed me from the womb as his servant, to gather Jacob and Israel to himself: I will be gathered and glorified before the Lord, and my God is my strength.

And he said to me, “It is a great thing for you to be called my servant, to establish the tribes of Jacob and bring back the scattered people of Israel. Look, I have appointed you as a covenant for the people and as a light for the nations, to bring salvation to the ends of the earth.”

Thus says the Lord who redeemed you, the God of Israel: “Sanctify the one who despises his own life, the one defiled by the nations, by the servants of rulers. Kings will see him and rise to their feet; rulers will bow down to him, because of the Lord, for the Holy One of Israel, who chose you, is faithful.”

Thus says the Lord to Israel: “At an acceptable time I heard you, and on the day of salvation I helped you. I formed you and gave you as a covenant for the nations, to establish the land and to assign the desolate inheritances,
to say to the prisoners, ‘Come out,’ and to those in darkness, ‘Show yourselves.’ They will graze along every road, and their pastures will be along every path.
They will neither hunger nor thirst, nor will they be scorched by the sun. Rather, the one who will have mercy on them will comfort them and lead them along springs of water.
I will turn all the mountains into a road and all the paths into their pastures.
Look, some will come from far away, some from the north and from the sea, and some from the land of Persia.”
Rejoice, heavens, and let the earth be glad. Let the mountains cry out with joy and the hills with righteousness, for God has had mercy on his people and has comforted the lowly among his people.
But Zion said, “The Lord has abandoned me, and God has forgotten me.”
“Can a woman forget her infant, or have no compassion on the child of her womb? Even if a woman forgets that child, I will not forget you,” says the Lord.
“Look, I have drawn your wall on my hands, and you are before me at all times.
You will quickly be rebuilt by those who tore you down, and those who devastated you will be driven away from you.

Lift up your eyes all around you and see them all, for look, they have gathered and come to you. As I live,” says the Lord, “you will wear them all like a robe and put them around you like a bride’s adornment.
For your desolate, ruined, and demolished places will now be too cramped for their inhabitants, and those who swallowed you up will go far away from you.”
For your sons whom you lost will say in your hearing, “This place is too cramped for us. Make room for us so that we may live here.”
And you will say in your heart, “Who bore these children for me? I was childless and widowed, a stranger and a captive. Who raised these children for me? I was left alone, and where were they?”

Thus says the Lord God: “Look, I will lift up my hand over the nations and raise my banner on the islands. They will bring your sons in their arms, and they will carry your daughters upon their shoulders.”

Kings will be your foster fathers, and their wives your nurses. They will bow down to you with their faces to the ground and lick the dust of your feet. You will know that I am the Lord, and those who wait for me will not be put to shame.
Can anyone take a giant’s plunder? Or can anyone take captives unjustly and escape?
Thus says the Lord: If anyone takes a giant captive, he will take his spoil, and whoever takes a giant’s spoil will escape safely. But I will render my judgment and rescue my sons.

Your oppressors will eat their own flesh and drink their own blood like new wine, and they will become drunk. All flesh will know that I am the Lord, who rescued you and helped you and strengthened Jacob.

Thus says the Lord: Where is the certificate of divorce with which I dismissed your mother? Or where is the merchants’ pledge by which I sold you? Rather, you were sold because of your sins, and because of your lawlessness I dismissed your mother.

For I came, and there was no one; I called, and there was no one to listen. Can my hand not rescue, or do I lack the power to save? Look, by my rebuke I will lay waste the sea and ruin the rivers. Their fish will dry up for lack of water and die of thirst.
I will clothe the heavens in darkness and make their covering like sackcloth.
The Lord God gives me a trained tongue, so that I may know how to speak a word at the right time. He prepared me morning after morning and gave me an ear to listen.
And the Lord’s instruction opens my ears, and I do not become stubborn or turn away in opposition.
I gave my back to blows and my cheeks to slaps, and I did not turn my face away from the shame of being spat in the face.
The Lord God became my helper; therefore I was not put to shame. Instead, I made my face like solid rock, and I knew that I would not be put to shame.
For the one who justifies me is near. Who is my adversary? Let him come and stand among us. And who is the one who judges me? Let him come near me.
For look, the Lord God is my helper. Who is there who will torment me? Look, all of you will wear out like rags, and a moth [?] will eat you.
Who among you fears the Lord? Let him listen to the voice of his servant. Those who walked in darkness and had no light, trust in the name of the Lord and take courage in God.

Look, all of you will be overcome by a blazing fire, as by a flame. You will walk in the light of your own fire and be set ablaze by its flame. This has come upon you because of me: you will lie down in sorrow.
Listen to me, you who pursue justice and seek the Lord. Look to the solid rock from which you were hewn and to the hollow of the pit from which you were dug.
Look to Abraham your father and to Sarah, who gave birth to you. For he was one man, and I called him and blessed him and made him numerous.

And now I will comfort you, Zion, and comfort all her ruined places. I will make all her ruined places like a garden and her western region like the garden of the Lord. Joy and gladness will be found in her, thanksgiving and the sound of praise.
Listen to me, listen to me, people, and you kings, pay attention to me, for laws will go out from me, and my judgment will be a light to the nations.
Quickly, quickly, my righteousness will draw near, and my salvation will come forth like light. The nations will put their hope in my arm; the islands will wait for me and put their hope in my arm.

Lift your eyes to the heavens and look at the earth below, for the heavens are established like smoke, and the earth will wear out like rags, and its inhabitants will perish in the same way. But my salvation will remain forever, and my righteousness will not fail.
Listen to me, you who know justice, my people, whose hearts hold my law. Do not fear people’s reproaches, and do not let their slanders put you to shame.
For they will wear out like rags over time and like wool eaten by a moth. But my righteousness will remain forever, and my salvation from generation to generation.

Awake, awake, Jerusalem, and clothe yourself with the strength of your arm. Awake as in the days of the beginning, as in the generations of old. Are you not the one who hewed down the expanse and drove away the dragon?
Are you not the one who laid waste the sea, the vast waters of the depths, who made the depths of the sea a road for the rescued and the saved to pass through?

For there will be a return from the Lord, and they will come to Zion with rejoicing and everlasting gladness. Blessing will be upon their heads, and joy will reach them; pain, sorrow, and sighing have been driven away.
I am, I am the very one who comforted you. Consider who you were, that you feared a mortal man and a son of man, who withered like grass.

You forgot God your Creator, who made the heavens and established the earth, and you were constantly afraid, all day long, of the fury of your oppressor as he planned to destroy you. And now, where is your oppressor’s fury?
For when you are delivered, he will not be able to stand, nor will he linger, nor will he kill you and bring you to destruction, and your bread will not fail.
I am the Lord your God, who stirs up the sea and makes its waves roar. The Lord of Hosts is my name.
I will put my words in your mouth and cover you under the shelter of my hand, with which I set up the heavens and laid the foundations of the earth, and I said to Zion, ‘You are my people.’
Awake, awake! Rise and stand, Jerusalem, you who drank from the Lord’s hand the cup of his anger, the cup of ruin, the cup of fury, which you drank and drained.
There was no one to comfort you among all the sons you bore, and no one to lend you a hand among all the sons you raised.
Two things confront you, and who will share your sorrow? Ruin and devastation, famine and sword—and who will comfort you?
Your sons are bewildered and lie asleep at the junctions of every road, like half-cooked beet greens. They are filled with the Lord’s anger, undone by the Lord God.
Therefore listen, you afflicted one, who are drunk, but not with wine.
Thus says the Lord God, who judges his people: ‘Look, I have taken from your hand the cup of ruin, the cup of my fury, and you will never drink it again.

I will put it into the hands of those who harm you and into the hands of those who afflicted you, who said to you, “Bow down so that we may pass over you.” And they laid your back level with the ground outside, for those passing over you.’
Awake, awake, Zion! Put on your strength, Zion, and put on your glory, Jerusalem, holy city, for the unclean and the uncircumcised will no longer pass through you.
Shake off your dust, rise and sit down, Jerusalem. Loosen the bond around your neck, captive daughter of Zion.
For thus says the Lord: ‘You were sold for nothing, and you will be redeemed without silver.’
Thus says the Lord: ‘My people first went down to the land of the Egyptians to live there as foreigners, and they were forcibly carried away to Assyria. And now, why are you here?’
Thus says the Lord: ‘My people were carried away for nothing; they were astonished and wept.’ Thus says the Lord: ‘Because of you, my name is continually blasphemed among the nations.’
Therefore my people will know my name on that day, that I am the very one of whom they spoke. And now I have come; I have arrived.
How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the messenger announcing peace, like a messenger of good things! For I will make your salvation heard, saying to Zion, ‘God will reign over you.’
For the voice of your watchmen has risen, and together they will rejoice with one voice, for they will see face to face the time when the Lord has mercy on Zion.
The mountains, together with the ruins of Jerusalem, will shout for joy, for the Lord has had mercy on her and redeemed Jerusalem.
The Lord will reveal his holy arm before all the nations, and all the ends of the earth will see the salvation of our God.
Depart, depart! Come out of there, and do not touch unclean things. Come out from among them and separate yourselves, you who carry the Lord’s vessels.
For you will not go out in turmoil or leave in flight, for the Lord himself will go before you, and the God of Israel is the one who gathers you.
Look, my servant will understand; he will be raised up and exalted and greatly glorified.
Just as many will be astonished at you, so your appearance will be stripped of beauty beyond that of other people, and your glory beyond that of the sons of men.
So many nations will marvel at you, and kings will shut their mouths, for those who were not told about him will see, and those who have not heard will understand.
Lord, who has believed our report, and to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?
We proclaimed him before him like a child, like a root in thirsty ground. He had no appearance or glory. We saw him, and he had no appearance or beauty.

But his appearance was dishonored, diminished beyond that of all the sons of men: a man under blows who knows how to endure pain. For he turned his face away, was dishonored, and was counted as nothing.
He bears our sins and suffers for us, yet we considered him to be in pain, under blows, and suffering as though from God.
But he was wounded for our sins and punished for our lawlessness. The discipline that brought us peace was upon him, and by his wounds we were healed.
We all wandered like sheep; each man wandered on his own path, and the Lord handed him over for our sins.
And in his suffering he does not open his mouth. He was led like a sheep to slaughter, and as a lamb stands silent before its shearer, so he does not open his mouth.
In his humiliation his judgment was taken away. Who will recount his lineage? For his life is taken from the earth; because of the lawlessness of my people he was led to death.
And I will give the wicked in exchange for his grave, and the powerful in exchange for his death, because he committed no lawlessness, and no deceit was found in his mouth.

And the Lord wishes to cleanse him of his wounds. If you give an offering for sins, your souls will see long-lived offspring. And the Lord wishes, through him, to lift him out of the suffering of his soul,
to show him light and form him with wisdom, to vindicate the righteous one who willingly served many; and he will take away their sins.

Therefore he will inherit many and divide the spoils of the mighty, because his soul was handed over to death and he was counted among the lawless. He took away the sins of many and was handed over because of their lawlessness.

Rejoice, barren woman who did not bear children! Shout and cry aloud, you who did not suffer labor pains! For the children of the deserted woman are more numerous than those of the woman who has a husband, for the Lord has spoken.
Enlarge the place of your tent and set up your pavilions. Do not hold back; lengthen your ropes and make your stakes firm.
You will spread out to the right and to the left. Your offspring will inherit the nations, and they will rebuild the ruined cities.

Do not be afraid because they put you to shame; do not be embarrassed because they disgraced you. For you will forget your lasting shame, and the disgrace of your widowhood will no longer be remembered by you.
For it is the Lord who does this for you; the Lord of Hosts is his name. And the one who redeemed you, the same God of Israel, will be called the God of all the earth.
The Lord did not call you as an abandoned, distressed wife, nor as a wife hated since her youth, but God said.
For a little while I abandoned you, but with great mercy I will have mercy on you.
For a brief moment of anger I turned my face away from you, but with everlasting mercy I will have mercy on you, says the Lord who redeemed you.
And this is to me like the floodwaters in Noah’s time: as I swore to him at that time not to be angry with the earth, so neither will I be angry with you.
Nor will I move the mountains or shift the hills with my threats. My mercy will not diminish toward you, and the covenant of your peace will not pass away, says the Lord.
I am reconciled with you, afflicted and shaken one, until you are comforted. Look, I have prepared your stones of ruby and your foundations of sapphire.
And I will erect your towers of jasper and your gates of crystal stones, and I will place around you a wall of the choicest precious stones.
And all your children will be taught by God, and your children will enjoy great peace.
And you shall be built up in righteousness. Keep far from injustice, and you shall not be afraid, and trembling shall not come near you.
For behold, newcomers shall draw near to you because of me; they shall dwell with you as foreigners and make you their refuge.
Behold, I established you, not like a smith who fans sparks with bellows and brings forth tools for work; rather, I established you, not for destruction and ruin.

No harmful weapon against you shall prosper, and you shall defeat every voice that rises against you in judgment, and all your accusers in that judgment. For this is the inheritance of the servants of the Lord, and you shall be righteous before me, says the Lord.
O you who are thirsty, go to the water; and all of you who have no money, go, buy and eat without money or payment for wine
and fat. Why indeed do you spend money on what is not bread, and your earnings on what does not satisfy? Listen to me and eat good things, and let your souls delight in goodness.
Listen with your ears; follow my ways. Listen to me, and your souls shall live in goodness. I will make an everlasting covenant with you, the faithful holy promises to David.
Behold, I gave him as a witness to the Gentiles, a ruler and commander of nations.
Nations that do not know you shall call to you, and peoples that did not recognize you shall make you their refuge, because of the Lord your God, the Holy One of Israel, for he has glorified you.
Seek the Lord, and when you find him, call to him, and when he draws near to you,
let the wicked abandon his ways, and the lawless man his thoughts. Let him return to the Lord and find mercy, and to our God, for he shall abundantly forgive your lawless deeds.
For my thoughts are not like your thoughts, and my ways are not like your ways, says the Lord.
