But as the heavens are far from the earth, so my ways are far from your ways, and my thoughts from your thoughts.
Just as rain or snow comes down from heaven and does not return there until it waters the earth, making it bear and sprout, and gives seed to the sower and bread for food,
so shall my word be that comes forth from my mouth. Let it not return empty until it accomplishes whatever I desire. And I shall make your ways easy, and you shall keep my ways.
For you will go out with joy and learn with gladness, for the mountains and hills will leap to welcome you joyfully, and all the trees of the forest will clap with their branches.
And instead of the thornbush, a cypress shall grow, and instead of the brier, a myrtle shall spring up. It shall be a name for the Lord and an everlasting sign, and it shall not cease.
Thus says the Lord: Observe justice and practice righteousness, for my salvation has come and is at hand, and my mercy is about to be revealed.
Blessed is the man who does this, and the person who remains steadfast in it, who keeps my Sabbaths and does not profane them, and keeps his hands from doing injustice.
Let not the foreigner who has come and joined himself to the Lord say, “The Lord will utterly exclude me from his people,” and let not the eunuch say, “I am a dry tree.”
Thus says the Lord to the eunuchs who keep my observances, choose what I desire, and remain steadfast in my covenant:
I shall give them in my house and within my walls a place of honor better than that of sons and daughters. I shall give them an everlasting name, and it shall not cease.

And the foreigners who have come and joined themselves to the Lord to serve him and love his name, to become his servants and maidservants, and all those who keep my Sabbaths and do not profane them, and remain steadfast in my covenant,

I will take them to my holy mountain and make them joyful in my house of prayer. Their burnt offerings and their sacrifices will be acceptable on my altar, for my house will be called a house of prayer for all nations.
The Lord God, who gathers the scattered people of Israel, said, “I will gather crowds to him.”
All you beasts of the wilderness, come and eat, all you beasts of the forest.
Look: they have all become blind, and none of them understands. They are all like mute dogs that cannot bark; they dream on their beds and love to doze.
They have become shameless dogs that never know when they have had enough. They are evil and have no understanding; all of them have gone their own ways.
Come, let us get wine and drink ourselves drunk, and let such a day be for us a great sacrifice, exceedingly abundant.

Do you see how the righteous person has perished, and no one takes it to heart? Righteous men are taken away, and no one considers that the righteous person is taken away from the presence of injustice.
Let his grave be in peace, for he has been taken away from their midst.
But you, come forward, lawless children, children born of prostitutes, children of adultery.
What are you boasting about? Against whom do you open your mouths, and at whom do you stick out your tongues? Are you not children of destruction, offspring of lawlessness?
You fell down and pleaded with your idols beneath densely growing trees. You sacrificed your children in deep ravines, among the rocky heights and along the sides of the valleys.
That is your portion, and that is your allotted share. To them you poured out offerings, and to them you presented sacrifices. Shall I not be angry over all this, says the Lord?
On the great and high mountain is your bed, and you went up there to offer sacrifices.

Behind the doorposts of your doors you set up your memorials. You thought that if you kept away from me, you would find something more. You widened your bed and stretched yourself out beside them; you loved your lovers.
You multiplied your acts of prostitution with them and brought yourself many lovers from distant places. You sent your messengers beyond your borders.

You were brought low and went down to the underworld. You grew weary through your many journeys, yet you did not say, ‘Now I will rest.’ For you did this with your own strength; therefore you did not submit to me.

Whom did you fear and dread, that you lied to me and did not remember me, did not bring me to mind, and did not keep me in your heart? I saw you and disregarded you. I am the one who has existed from eternity, yet you did not fear me.
Now I will declare my righteousness and your evil deeds, which will not help you.

When you cry out, they will not save you from your distress, for winds will carry them all away, and storms will scatter them. But those who put their hope in me will possess the land and inherit my holy mountain.
They will say, ‘Make the roads smooth before him, and remove obstacles and stumbling blocks from the road of my people.’

Thus says the Most High, who dwells in the heights forever, the Holy One among the holy ones, whose name is exalted and who rests among the holy: he gives patience to those in doubt and life to those whose hearts are worn down.
And I will not seek vengeance against you forever, nor will I be [?] angry with you, for a spirit will go out from me, and I made every breath.
Because of his sins I grieved him for a little while. I struck him and turned my face away from him. He was grieved and went sorrowfully before me along his ways.
I saw the ways of his heart and healed him. I comforted him and gave him true consolation, and also to those who mourn for him.
I established the fruit of peace upon peace for those far away and those nearby, says the Lord, and I will heal them.
But the lawless will toss like the sea and find no rest, and its water will perish in trampling and mud.
There is no peace for the ungodly, says the Lord.
Cry out with strength and do not hold back. Raise your voice like a trumpet. Tell my people their sins and the house of Jacob their lawless deeds.

They seek me day after day and desire to know my ways, like a people who have practiced righteousness and have not abandoned the judgments of their God. Now they come and ask for righteous judgments; they long to draw near to God.

They say, ‘Why have we fasted, and you have not seen? Why have we humbled ourselves, and you have not noticed?’ Because on your fasting days your own desires are fulfilled, and you torment everyone who is under your authority.
You fast amid disputes and quarrels, and you strike the lowly. What use to me is a fast on such a day, when you come to appeal to me and I do not listen to you?

I did not choose such a fast, nor a day on which a person weakens himself. Even if you bend your neck like a hoop and spread sackcloth and ashes beneath you, I did not call that a fast or an acceptable day. I did not choose such a fast, says the Lord.
Instead, loosen the knot of injustice, undo the deceit of your oppressive dealings, release the afflicted with a pardon, and tear up every unjust bond of debt.
Break your bread for the hungry, and bring the homeless poor into your house. If you see someone naked, clothe them, and do not turn your eyes away from your own kin.
Then your light will spread at dawn, and your healing will come quickly. Your righteousness will go before you, and the glory of God will surround you.

Then you will call, and God will hear you. While you are still speaking, he will say, “Here I am; I have come.” And if you remove from yourself the knot of injustice, violence, and words of grumbling,
and give your bread to the hungry wholeheartedly and satisfy those in need, then your light will rise in the darkness, and your darkness will be like midday.

And your God will be with you at all times, and your soul will be filled according to its desire, and your bones will grow fat. They will be like a well-watered garden and like a spring whose water never fails.

And your ancient ruins will be rebuilt, and your foundations will be everlasting; you will raise them up from generation to generation. You will be called Repairer of the Breach in the Fence, and you will put an end to the paths between them.

If you turn back your foot so as not to do your own will on the holy day, and call the Sabbaths delightful, consecrated to God and honored, and do not turn your foot toward work or speak any angry word with your mouth, you will place your hope in the Lord.
And he will bring you into the good things of the land and feed you with the inheritance of Jacob your father, for the mouth of the Lord has spoken this.
Is the hand of the Lord unable to save, or has he made his ear heavy so that he cannot hear?
Rather, your sins separate you from God, and because of your lawless deeds he has turned his face away from you, so as not to show mercy.
For your hands are defiled with blood, and your fingers with sins. Your lips have spoken lawlessness, and your tongues devise injustice.
There is no one who speaks righteousness, and there are no truthful judgments. They trust in empty things and speak falsehood, for they conceive troubles and give birth to lawlessness.
They broke open vipers’ eggs and weave spiders’ webs. Whoever wished to eat one of them broke it open and found water, and in it a viper.
Their webs will not become cloth, nor will they clothe themselves with the works of their own hands, because their works are works of lawlessness, and deeds of injustice are in their hands.
Their feet run toward evil; they hurry to shed innocent blood. Their thoughts are the thoughts of fools; destruction and misery are in their ways.
And they have not known the way of peace, and there is no justice in their ways, for the paths they walk are crooked, and they have not known peace.
Therefore justice has departed from them, and may righteousness not reach them. While they looked for light, darkness came upon them, and while they waited for it, they walked in gloom.
They will feel the walls like blind people and grope like [?]. They will stumble at midday as though it were the middle of the night, and struggle for breath like people at death’s door.
And they will all move along like bears and like doves. We stood waiting for justice, but there was none, and for salvation, but it withdrew from us.
For our lawless deeds are many before you, and our sins have stood against us. Our lawless deeds are within us, and we ourselves know our injustices.
We acted wickedly and lied to the Lord, and turned back from our God. We spoke injustice and rebelled; we conceived and pondered words of injustice in our hearts.
We pushed justice back, and righteousness withdrew from us, for truth vanished from their roads, and they could not walk along the straight path, and righteousness was taken away from them.
They turned their hearts away from understanding. The Lord saw and was displeased, because there was no justice.
He looked, and there was no one; he saw, and there was no one to help. He repaid them with his own arm and upheld them according to his mercy.
He put on righteousness like armor and placed salvation on his head like a helmet. He wrapped himself in clothing and a robe of vengeance, to repay what was due,
and disgrace to his adversaries; he will repay the islands what is due.
In the west they will fear the name of the Lord, and in the east his glorious name, for wrath will come like a violent river; it will come from the Lord in fury.
A deliverer will come from Zion and turn away the ungodliness of Jacob, says the Lord.

And this is my covenant with them, says the Lord: My Spirit, which is upon you, and the words that I have put in your mouth shall not depart from your mouth, or from the mouth of your offspring, or from the mouth of your offspring’s offspring, says the Lord, from now on and forever.
Shine, shine, Jerusalem, for your light has arrived, and the glory of the Lord will rise upon you.
For behold, darkness has covered the earth, and thick gloom the nations; but the Lord will reveal himself upon you, and his glory will appear upon you.
Kings will walk in your light, and nations in the rising of your light.
Lift up your eyes all around you and see all your children gathered to you. Your sons have come and arrived from far away, and your daughters will be brought, carried upon their shoulders.
Then you will see and rejoice; you will fear and tremble in your heart, because the wealth of the sea, of nations, and of peoples will be transferred to you.

Herds of camels will come to you, and the camel herds of Midian and Ephah will cover you. They will all come from Sheba, bringing gold, frankincense, and precious stones, and they will bring the good news of the Lord’s salvation.
All the flocks of Kedar will gather to you, and the rams of Nebaioth will be brought and offered as an acceptable sacrifice upon my altar, and my house of prayer will be glorified.
Who are these who have flown like clouds and come to me like doves in flocks with their young?

The islands wait for me, and the ships of Tarshish will be first to bring your sons from far away, with their silver and gold, for the name of the holy Lord and for the glorification of the Holy One of Israel.
And the sons of foreigners will build your walls, and their kings will offer themselves to you, for in my anger I struck you, and in my mercy I loved you.
Your gates will remain open continually, by day and by night, and will not be shut, so that the wealth of the nations may be brought to you; and they will bring their kings to you.
For the nations and kings that will not serve you will perish, and those nations will be utterly devastated.
The glory of Lebanon will come to you, with [?], plane trees, cypresses, and cedars together, to glorify the place of my sanctuary; and I will glorify the place of my feet.

The sons of those who oppressed and provoked you will come to you trembling, and all who terrified you will bow down at the soles of your feet. You will be called the city of the Lord, Zion of the Holy One of Israel.
Because you were abandoned and hated, and there was no one to help you, I will make you an everlasting joy, a delight from generation to generation.
You will suck the milk of the nations and consume the wealth of kings, and you will know that I am the Lord who saves and redeems you, the God of Israel.

Instead of bronze I will bring you gold, and instead of iron I will bring you silver. Instead of wood I will bring you bronze, and instead of stone I will give you iron. I will make your rulers peace and your overseers righteousness.
Injustice will no longer be heard of in your land, nor destruction and misery within your borders. Instead, your walls will be called Salvation, and your gates Rejoicing.
The sun will no longer be your light by day, nor will the shining moon give you light at night. Instead, the Lord will be your everlasting light, and God will be your glory.
Your sun will not set, and your moon will not fail you, for the Lord will be your everlasting light, and the days of your mourning will end.
All your people will be righteous, and they will inherit the land forever, preserving the new planting, the work of their hands, for glory.
The few will become a thousand, and the smallest will become a great nation, for I, the Lord, will gather them at the appointed times.
The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me to bring good news to the poor. He has sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to proclaim release to captives and sight to the blind,
to proclaim the Lord’s favorable year and the day of recompense from our God, to comfort all who mourn,

to give the mourners of Zion glory instead of ashes, an anointing of joy, and to the mourners a garment of glory instead of spirits of despair. They will be called generations of righteousness, a planting of the Lord for glory.
They will rebuild the ancient ruins and raise up the places devastated long ago. They will restore the ruined cities, devastated from generation to generation.
Foreigners will come as shepherds of your flocks, and people of other nations will be your plowmen and vineyard workers.
But you will be called priests of the Lord and named ministers of our God. You will consume the wealth of the nations, and through their greatness you will become magnificent.
Instead of your shame you will have double joy, and instead of your dishonor, gladness. Then they will inherit the land a second time, and everlasting joy will be upon their heads.
For I am the Lord, who loves justice and hates robbery born of injustice. I will give the righteous their wages and make an everlasting covenant with them.
Their offspring will be known among the nations, and their descendants among the peoples. Everyone who sees them will recognize that they are offspring blessed by God.

They will rejoice greatly in the Lord; my soul will exult in the Lord, for he has clothed me in a garment of salvation and a robe of joy. Like a bridegroom, he has placed a crown on me, and like a bride, he has adorned me with ornaments.
As the earth makes its flowers grow, and as a garden makes its seeds sprout, so the Lord will cause his righteousness and gladness to spring forth before all the nations.
For Zion’s sake I will not be silent, and for Jerusalem’s sake I will not rest, until her righteousness shines like light and her salvation blazes like lightning.
The nations will see your righteousness, and all kings your glory. You will be called by a new name that the Lord will give you.
You will be a crown of beauty in the Lord’s hand and a royal diadem in the hand of your God.

You will no longer be called Forsaken, and your land will no longer be called Desolate. Instead, you will be named My Delight, and your land Inhabited Settlement, for the Lord will delight in you, and your land will teem with inhabitants.
As a young man lives with a virgin, so your sons will live in you. As a bridegroom rejoices over his bride, so the Lord will rejoice over you.
Upon your walls, Jerusalem, I have stationed watchmen, who throughout the whole day and all night must never cease remembering the Lord.
For there is no one like you, if he restores Jerusalem and makes her a source of pride upon the earth.
The Lord has sworn by his glory and by the strength of his arm: I will not give your wheat and food into the hands of your enemies, nor will foreigners drink your wine, for which you have labored.
But those who gathered it will eat it and bless the Lord, and those who collected it will drink it in the halls of my holy places.
Go, enter through my gates. Prepare the roads, level the paths, make a road for my people, and remove the stones from the road. Raise a banner among the nations.
For behold, the Lord has made this heard to the ends of the earth: Say to the daughter of Zion, “Behold, your Savior is arriving. He has his reward with him, and his work is before him.”
He will call them a holy people, redeemed by the Lord, and you will be called a sought-after city, and not abandoned.
Who is this who comes striding from Edom, with red garments from Bozrah, in a beautiful robe and with mighty strength? “I proclaim righteousness and the justice of salvation.”
Why are your garments red, and your clothes like those of someone who has trodden a full winepress?
I trod the winepress alone, and no one from the nations was with me. I trampled them in my fury and crushed them in my anger. I brought them down to the earth and stained all my clothes.
For the day of retribution had come upon them, and the year of salvation had arrived.
I looked, and there was no one to help. I considered, and there was no one to come to my support. My own arm saved them, and my anger alone stood by me.
I trampled them in my anger and slaughtered them in my fury, and brought them down to the earth.

I will remember the Lord’s mercies and recall the Lord’s might, for everything the Lord grants us—the Lord, the judge, the benefactor of the house of Israel, who bestows these things on us according to his mercy and his abundant righteousness.
He said, “They are my people, my children, and they will not dishonor me.” And he became their salvation from all their affliction.

It was neither a messenger nor an angel, but the Lord himself who saved them. Because he loved them and had compassion on them, he himself saved them, lifted them up, and carried them all the days of old.
But they rebelled and angered his Holy Spirit. The Lord turned against them as an enemy; he himself waged war against them.
And he remembered the days of old: “Where are Moses and his people, who brought the shepherd of the flocks up from the earth? Where is the one who put the Holy Spirit in them?”
He who lifted up Moses with his right hand, whose glorious arm subdued the waters before him, to make an everlasting name for himself.
He led them through the depths like a horse through the wilderness,
and like an animal across a plain, and they did not grow weary. The Spirit from the Lord descended and led them. Thus you led your people to make a glorious name for yourself.
And now turn from heaven and look from your holy temple and from your glory. Where are your zeal and your power? Where is the abundant mercy of your compassion, with which you used to forgive us?
For you are our Father. Abraham did not know us, and Israel did not recognize us, but you, Lord, are our Father. Save us, for from the beginning your name has been upon us.
Why have you led us astray from your ways, Lord, and hardened our hearts so that we do not fear you? Return for the sake of your servants; return for the sake of the tribes of your inheritance.
Perhaps we will not inherit your holy mountain. Our adversaries oppressed us and trampled your sanctuary.
We have become as we were at first, when you did not rule over us and your name was not called upon us.
If you open the heavens, the mountains will tremble before you and melt like wax before fire.
Fire will burn your adversaries, and your name will become known to your opponents, and the nations will be shaken before you.
When you perform glorious deeds, the mountains will tremble before you.
From ages past we have not heard, nor have our eyes seen, any God besides you, or your works that you will do for those who wait for your mercy.
For he will meet those who do what is right, and they will remember your ways. Now behold, you became angry, and we sinned; because of this we went astray.
We all became like unclean people, and all our righteousness was like menstrual cloths. We all fell like leaves; because of our lawless deeds, winds drove us away.
And there will be no one who calls upon your name, nor anyone who remembers to take refuge in you, for you have turned your face away from us and handed us over because of our sins.
And now, Lord, you are our Father. We are clay, and you are our Maker; we are all the work of your hands.
Do not be exceedingly angry with us, Lord, and do not remember our sins when the time comes. And now look, Lord, for we are all your people.
Your holy city, Zion, became a ruin; Jerusalem became like a wilderness and was handed over to curses.
Our holy house and our glory, which our fathers praised, were burned down, and all our splendor was destroyed.
And in the face of all this, do you hold back, Lord, and have you remained silent and humbled us so greatly?
I revealed myself to those who did not ask about me; I was found by those who did not seek me. I said, “Here I am,” to a nation that did not call upon my name.
All day long I stretched out my hand to a disobedient and defiant people, who walked on a path that was not good, but followed their own sins.
This people continually provoked me to anger before my face. They offered sacrifices in their gardens and burned incense on their bricks to demons whom they did not remember.
They lie down and sleep in caves to see dreams. They ate pork and broth from sacrifices, and all their vessels were defiled.
They said, “Stay away from me; do not come near me, for I am holy.” This is the smoke of my anger, in which a fire burns all day long.
Look, it is written before me: I will not be silent until I repay them into their laps
for their sins and the sins of their fathers together, says the Lord. They burned incense on the mountains and insulted me on the hills. I will first repay their deeds into their laps.

This is what the Lord says: Just as, when a grape is found in a cluster, people say, “Do not destroy it, for the Lord’s blessing is in it,” so I will act for the sake of my servants, and because of this I will not destroy them all.
I will bring forth offspring from Jacob and Judah, and they will inherit my holy mountain. My chosen ones will inherit it, and my servants will live there.
There will be a fold for shepherds in the woodland, and the valley of Achor will be a resting place for the herds of my people who sought me.
But you abandoned me and forgot my holy mountain. You prepared a table for demons and mixed drinks for Fortune.
I will hand you over to the sword, and you will all be slaughtered, because I called you and you did not listen; I spoke and you defied me. You did evil before me and chose what I did not desire.

Therefore this is what the Lord says: Look, those who serve me will eat, but you will hunger. Look, those who serve me will drink, but you will thirst. Look, those who serve me will rejoice, but you will be ashamed.
Look, those who serve me will exult with joy in their hearts, but you will cry out because of the pain in your hearts and mourn because of your broken spirits.
For you will leave your name as a source of satisfaction for my chosen ones, and the Lord will destroy you. My servants will be called by a new name,

which will be blessed on earth, for they will bless the true God. Those who swear oaths on earth will swear by the true God, for they will forget their former afflictions, and these will no longer come into their hearts.
For there will be new heavens and a new earth. They will no longer remember the former things, nor will these come into their hearts.
Instead, they will find joy and gladness in what I will establish. For look, I am making Jerusalem a delight and my people a joy.
I will delight in Jerusalem and rejoice over my people. No longer will the sound of weeping or the sound of lamentation be heard there.

There shall be no one there who dies before his time, nor an old man who has not completed his years, for the youngest child shall be a hundred years old, and whoever dies at a hundred shall be called sinful and accursed.
They shall build houses and live in them themselves; they shall plant vineyards and eat their fruit themselves.
They shall no longer build for others to inhabit, or plant for others to eat. The days of my people shall be like the days of the tree of life, and the works of their hands shall endure into old age.
My chosen ones shall no longer labor in vain, nor bear children under a curse, for they are offspring blessed by God, and their descendants shall be with them.
Before they have called, I will hear them, and while they are still speaking, I will say, “What are you asking for?”

At that time wolves and lambs shall graze together, and the lion shall eat straw like an ox, and the serpent shall eat dust like bread. They shall neither do wrong nor cause harm on my holy mountain, says the Lord.
Thus says the Lord: Heaven is my throne, and the earth is the footstool of my feet. What kind of house will you build for me, says the Lord, or what kind of place will be my resting place?
For my hand made all these things, and everything is mine, says the Lord. And to whom shall I look, if not to the meek and humble and to the one who trembles at my words?

But the lawless person who offers me an ox as a sacrifice is like someone who strikes a human being’s skull. Whoever offers a sheep as a sacrifice is like someone who slaughters a dog, and whoever offers fine flour is like someone who pours out pig’s blood. Whoever offers frankincense as memorial incense is like a blasphemer. They themselves chose their own ways and the abominations in which their souls delighted.

And I will take their deceptions in hand and repay them according to their sins, for I called them and they did not hear me; I spoke and they did not listen. They did evil before me and chose what I did not desire.

Hear the words of the Lord, you who tremble at his words. Speak, our brothers, to those who hate you and despise you, so that the name of the Lord may be glorified and he may appear in your joy, and they shall be ashamed.
A sound of shouting from the city, a voice from the temple, the voice of the Lord, who repays his adversaries!
Before the pregnant woman had given birth, and before the pains of labor had come, she was delivered and bore a male child.
Who has heard or seen anything like this? Did the earth go into labor in a single day and give birth to an entire nation all at once? For Zion went into labor and bore her children.
I gave you this hope, and you did not remember me, says the Lord. Did I not make both the barren woman and the woman who bears children, says your God?
Rejoice, Jerusalem, and gather to celebrate a festival in her, all of you who love her. Be glad and rejoice together, you who sit in mourning for her.
So that you may nurse and be satisfied at the breasts of her consolation, and fully enjoy the coming of her glory.

For thus says the Lord: Behold, I will turn peace toward them like a river, and the glory of the nations like an overflowing torrent. They shall carry their children lifted upon their shoulders and cradle them on their knees.
As a mother cradles her child, so I will cradle you, and you shall be comforted in Jerusalem.
You shall see, and your hearts shall rejoice, and your bones shall flourish like green grass. The hand of the Lord shall be made known to those who fear him, and he shall threaten the unbelievers.
For behold, the Lord shall come like fire, and his chariots like a whirlwind, to bring his retribution in fury and his rebukes in flames of fire.
For by the Lord’s fire the whole earth will be judged, and by his sword all flesh. Many will be wounded by the Lord.
Those who sanctify and purify themselves in their gardens and halls, who eat pig’s flesh, abominable things, and mice, shall all perish together, says the Lord.
And I know their deeds and their thoughts. I come to gather all nations and languages; they will come and see my glory.

And I will set a sign upon them, and I will send survivors from among them to the nations—to Tarshish, Pul, Lud, Meshech, Tubal, Greece, and the distant islands whose people have not heard my name or seen my glory. They will proclaim my glory and my name among the nations.

And they will bring their brothers from all the nations as an offering to the Lord, riding in chariots, with harnessed horses and canopies, to the holy city of Jerusalem, says the Lord, just as the children of Israel brought me their offerings with psalms in the house of the Lord.
And from among them I will take priests and Levites for myself, says the Lord.
Just as the new heavens and the new earth that I make will remain before me, says the Lord, so your offspring will remain.
And month by month and Sabbath by Sabbath, all flesh will come to worship before me in Jerusalem, says the Lord God.
And they will go out and see the bones of the people who transgressed against me, for their worm will not die and their fire will not be quenched, and they will be a spectacle to all flesh.
